cuCheckpointOperationComplete.doc:
Complete a custom-storage checkpoint or restore operation.

After [cuCheckpointProcessCheckpoint](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__CHECKPOINT.html#group__cuda__checkpoint_1ga362df3bb9722295885b7ec3501dd623d) or [cuCheckpointProcessRestore](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__CHECKPOINT.html#group__cuda__checkpoint_1gaf2066439091dfa0eae0cbca0144f5e91) with custom storage, [cuCheckpointOperationComplete](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__CHECKPOINT.html#group__cuda__checkpoint_1ga6627f44a0c8f3e7f470091269b9e07d5) should be called when the application has finished or enqueued (on a stream) the required copies (for checkpoint, GPU mappings to custom storage and for restore, custom storage into GPU mappings) so the driver can finish the operation.

[cuCheckpointOperationComplete](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__CHECKPOINT.html#group__cuda__checkpoint_1ga6627f44a0c8f3e7f470091269b9e07d5) will first synchronize on the streams returned by [cuCheckpointProcessCheckpoint](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__CHECKPOINT.html#group__cuda__checkpoint_1ga362df3bb9722295885b7ec3501dd623d) or [cuCheckpointProcessRestore](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__CHECKPOINT.html#group__cuda__checkpoint_1gaf2066439091dfa0eae0cbca0144f5e91). The driver assumes that the application has completed copying the memory to or from custom storage once synchronization is done. None of the streams returned by [cuCheckpointProcessCheckpoint](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__CHECKPOINT.html#group__cuda__checkpoint_1ga362df3bb9722295885b7ec3501dd623d) or [cuCheckpointProcessRestore](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__CHECKPOINT.html#group__cuda__checkpoint_1gaf2066439091dfa0eae0cbca0144f5e91) should be in stream capture mode; any attempt to do so would result in [CUDA_ERROR_STREAM_CAPTURE_UNSUPPORTED](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggac6c391505e117393cc2558fff6bfc2e9aadf26f72a5e6589c7ade9af3b1b62e3d). Once the synchronization is done, [cuCheckpointOperationComplete](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__CHECKPOINT.html#group__cuda__checkpoint_1ga6627f44a0c8f3e7f470091269b9e07d5) will unmap the GPU memory that was mapped on each GPU in a particular [cuCheckpointProcessCheckpoint](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__CHECKPOINT.html#group__cuda__checkpoint_1ga362df3bb9722295885b7ec3501dd623d) or [cuCheckpointProcessRestore](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__CHECKPOINT.html#group__cuda__checkpoint_1gaf2066439091dfa0eae0cbca0144f5e91) operation. [cuCheckpointOperationComplete](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__CHECKPOINT.html#group__cuda__checkpoint_1ga6627f44a0c8f3e7f470091269b9e07d5) identifies the operation to be completed using `handle`. This handle is set by [cuCheckpointProcessCheckpoint](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__CHECKPOINT.html#group__cuda__checkpoint_1ga362df3bb9722295885b7ec3501dd623d) or [cuCheckpointProcessRestore](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__CHECKPOINT.html#group__cuda__checkpoint_1gaf2066439091dfa0eae0cbca0144f5e91).

When the call returns successfully, the target process will be in the [CU_PROCESS_STATE_CHECKPOINTED](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggac96cdda177a2b8c296144567cbea4f23a268c54df6d4456f1389187e34012f782) state when completing a checkpoint operation or the [CU_PROCESS_STATE_LOCKED](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggac96cdda177a2b8c296144567cbea4f23ad8c164cf538d07ab27ba2de6356302dd) state when completing a restore operation.

cuCheckpointProcessCheckpoint.doc:
Checkpoint a CUDA process’s GPU memory contents.

Checkpoints a CUDA process specified by `pid`. The GPU memory contents will be brought into host memory or mapped onto the calling process’s GPUs for user-defined behavior. Underlying GPU references are released when checkpointing completes. The process must be in the [CU_PROCESS_STATE_LOCKED](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggac96cdda177a2b8c296144567cbea4f23ad8c164cf538d07ab27ba2de6356302dd) state to checkpoint.

When [CUcheckpointCheckpointArgs::customStorageInfo_out](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/structCUcheckpointCheckpointArgs.html#structcucheckpointcheckpointargs_1ac3c629ce05a8d1e251f4bda72050f183) is not NULL, all the GPU memory allocated by the process with `pid` will be mapped onto the calling process’s GPUs so the application can copy the memory to custom storage. Upon return of this call, the pointer referenced by [CUcheckpointCheckpointArgs::customStorageInfo_out](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/structCUcheckpointCheckpointArgs.html#structcucheckpointcheckpointargs_1ac3c629ce05a8d1e251f4bda72050f183) will point to a [CUcheckpointCustomStorageInfo](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/structCUcheckpointCustomStorageInfo.html#structcucheckpointcustomstorageinfo) struct allocated and populated by the driver. For each GPU which contains data from the checkpointed process, there is a corresponding entry in the [CUcheckpointCustomStoragePerDeviceData](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/structCUcheckpointCustomStoragePerDeviceData.html#structcucheckpointcustomstorageperdevicedata) array.

The application is responsible for copying the mapped data from the GPU at the specified device address to custom storage. When checkpointing to custom storage, the application is expected to call [cuCheckpointOperationComplete](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__CHECKPOINT.html#group__cuda__checkpoint_1ga6627f44a0c8f3e7f470091269b9e07d5). The [CUcheckpointCustomStorageInfo::handle](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/structCUcheckpointCustomStorageInfo.html#structcucheckpointcustomstorageinfo_1a9095a23e289a5e9f42b9ce9949d04d2c) set by this call should be passed to [cuCheckpointOperationComplete](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__CHECKPOINT.html#group__cuda__checkpoint_1ga6627f44a0c8f3e7f470091269b9e07d5) in `handle`. The driver synchronizes all the streams in [cuCheckpointOperationComplete](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__CHECKPOINT.html#group__cuda__checkpoint_1ga6627f44a0c8f3e7f470091269b9e07d5), at which point the copy to custom storage is considered complete.

When checkpointing to custom storage, the application is expected to retain primary contexts of all the devices used by the process to be checkpointed. Otherwise [cuCheckpointProcessCheckpoint](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__CHECKPOINT.html#group__cuda__checkpoint_1ga362df3bb9722295885b7ec3501dd623d) will return [CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_CONTEXT](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggac6c391505e117393cc2558fff6bfc2e9aa484e9af32c1e9893ff21f0e0191a12d). Unlike other checkpoint operations, checkpointing to custom storage requires [cuInit](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__INITIALIZE.html#group__cuda__initialize_1ga0a2f1517e1bd8502c7194c3a8c134bc3) to have been called before execution. Checkpointing the calling process’s GPU memory to custom storage is not supported. Upon successful return, the target process will be in the [CU_PROCESS_STATE_CHECKPOINTING](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggac96cdda177a2b8c296144567cbea4f23a86afdd379414417a4c12732eb345ace6) state.

When [CUcheckpointCheckpointArgs::customStorageInfo_out](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/structCUcheckpointCheckpointArgs.html#structcucheckpointcheckpointargs_1ac3c629ce05a8d1e251f4bda72050f183) is NULL, the GPU memory contents will be brought into host memory by [cuCheckpointProcessCheckpoint](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__CHECKPOINT.html#group__cuda__checkpoint_1ga362df3bb9722295885b7ec3501dd623d). The application is not expected to copy the GPU memory contents. The application is also not expected to call [cuCheckpointOperationComplete](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__CHECKPOINT.html#group__cuda__checkpoint_1ga6627f44a0c8f3e7f470091269b9e07d5). Upon successful return, the target process will be in the [CU_PROCESS_STATE_CHECKPOINTED](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggac96cdda177a2b8c296144567cbea4f23a268c54df6d4456f1389187e34012f782) state.

pid.doc: The process ID of the CUDA process.

cuCheckpointProcessGetRestoreThreadId.doc:
Returns the restore thread ID for a CUDA process.

Returns in `*tid` the thread ID of the CUDA restore thread for the process specified by `pid`.

pid.doc: The process ID of the CUDA process.

cuCheckpointProcessGetState.doc:
Returns the process state of a CUDA process.

Returns in `*state` the current state of the CUDA process specified by `pid`.

pid.doc: The process ID of the CUDA process.

cuCheckpointProcessLock.doc:
Lock a running CUDA process.

Lock the CUDA process specified by `pid` which will block further CUDA API calls. Process must be in the RUNNING state in order to lock.

Upon successful return the process will be in the LOCKED state.

If timeoutMs is specified and the timeout is reached the process will be left in the RUNNING state upon return.

pid.doc: The process ID of the CUDA process.

cuCheckpointProcessRestore.doc:
Restore a CUDA process’s GPU memory contents from its last checkpoint.

Restores a CUDA process specified by `pid` from its last checkpoint. Process must be in the [CU_PROCESS_STATE_CHECKPOINTED](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggac96cdda177a2b8c296144567cbea4f23a268c54df6d4456f1389187e34012f782) state to restore.

GPU UUID pairs can be specified in `args` to remap the process old GPUs onto new GPUs. The GPU to restore onto needs to have enough memory and be of the same chip type as the old GPU. If an array of GPU UUID pairs is specified, it must contain every checkpointed GPU.

CUDA process restore requires persistence mode to be enabled or [cuInit](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__INITIALIZE.html#group__cuda__initialize_1ga0a2f1517e1bd8502c7194c3a8c134bc3) to have been called before execution.

When [CUcheckpointRestoreArgs::customStorageInfo_out](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/structCUcheckpointRestoreArgs.html#structcucheckpointrestoreargs_1a0dcad30bf1005161fe90f512da4b9aec) is not NULL, all the GPU memory to be restored for the process with `pid` will be mapped onto the calling process’s GPUs so the application can copy the memory back to the GPU.

Upon return of this call, the pointer referenced by [CUcheckpointRestoreArgs::customStorageInfo_out](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/structCUcheckpointRestoreArgs.html#structcucheckpointrestoreargs_1a0dcad30bf1005161fe90f512da4b9aec) will point to a [CUcheckpointCustomStorageInfo](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/structCUcheckpointCustomStorageInfo.html#structcucheckpointcustomstorageinfo) struct allocated and populated by the driver. For each GPU which contains data from the restored process, there is a corresponding entry in the [CUcheckpointCustomStoragePerDeviceData](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/structCUcheckpointCustomStoragePerDeviceData.html#structcucheckpointcustomstorageperdevicedata) array.

The application is responsible for copying the data from custom storage to the GPU at the specified device address. When restoring from custom storage, the application is expected to call [cuCheckpointOperationComplete](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__CHECKPOINT.html#group__cuda__checkpoint_1ga6627f44a0c8f3e7f470091269b9e07d5). The [CUcheckpointCustomStorageInfo::handle](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/structCUcheckpointCustomStorageInfo.html#structcucheckpointcustomstorageinfo_1a9095a23e289a5e9f42b9ce9949d04d2c) set by this call should be passed to [cuCheckpointOperationComplete](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__CHECKPOINT.html#group__cuda__checkpoint_1ga6627f44a0c8f3e7f470091269b9e07d5) in `handle`. The driver synchronizes all the streams in [cuCheckpointOperationComplete](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__CHECKPOINT.html#group__cuda__checkpoint_1ga6627f44a0c8f3e7f470091269b9e07d5), at which point the copy from custom storage is considered complete.

When restoring from custom storage, the application is expected to retain primary contexts of all the devices used by the process to be restored. Otherwise [cuCheckpointProcessRestore](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__CHECKPOINT.html#group__cuda__checkpoint_1gaf2066439091dfa0eae0cbca0144f5e91) will return [CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_CONTEXT](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggac6c391505e117393cc2558fff6bfc2e9aa484e9af32c1e9893ff21f0e0191a12d)

. Restoring the calling process’s

GPU memory from custom storage is not supported. Upon successful return, the target process will be in the

When [CUcheckpointRestoreArgs::customStorageInfo_out](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/structCUcheckpointRestoreArgs.html#structcucheckpointrestoreargs_1a0dcad30bf1005161fe90f512da4b9aec) is NULL, the GPU memory contents will be restored from host memory by [cuCheckpointProcessRestore](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__CHECKPOINT.html#group__cuda__checkpoint_1gaf2066439091dfa0eae0cbca0144f5e91). The application is not expected to copy back the GPU memory contents. The application is also not expected to call [cuCheckpointOperationComplete](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__CHECKPOINT.html#group__cuda__checkpoint_1ga6627f44a0c8f3e7f470091269b9e07d5). Upon successful return, the target process will be in the [CU_PROCESS_STATE_LOCKED](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggac96cdda177a2b8c296144567cbea4f23ad8c164cf538d07ab27ba2de6356302dd) state.

pid.doc: The process ID of the CUDA process.

cuCheckpointProcessUnlock.doc:
Unlock a CUDA process to allow CUDA API calls.

Unlocks a process specified by `pid` allowing it to resume making CUDA API calls. Process must be in the LOCKED state.

Upon successful return the process will be in the RUNNING state.

pid.doc: The process ID of the CUDA process.

cuCtxCreate.signature: CUresult cuCtxCreate(CUcontext * pctx, CUctxCreateParams * ctxCreateParams, unsigned int flags, CUdevice dev)
cuCtxCreate.doc:
Create a CUDA context.

Creates a new CUDA context and associates it with the calling thread. The `flags` parameter is described below. The context is created with a usage count of 1 and the caller of cuCtxCreate() must call cuCtxDestroy() when done using the context. If a context is already current to the thread, it is supplanted by the newly created context and may be restored by a subsequent call to cuCtxPopCurrent().

A regular CUDA context can be created by setting `ctxCreateParams` to NULL.

A CUDA context can be created with execution affinity. The type and the amount of execution resource the context can use is limited by `paramsArray` and `numExecAffinityParams` in `execAffinity`. The `paramsArray` is an array of `CUexecAffinityParam` and the `numExecAffinityParams` describes the size of the paramsArray. If two `CUexecAffinityParam` in the array have the same type, the latter execution affinity parameter overrides the former execution affinity parameter. The supported execution affinity types are:

A CUDA context can be created in CIG(CUDA in Graphics) mode by setting `cigParams`. Data from graphics client is shared with CUDA via the `sharedData` in `cigParams`. Support for D3D12 graphics client can be determined using [cuDeviceGetAttribute()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__DEVICE.html#group__cuda__device_1ga9c3e1414f0ad901d3278a4d6645fc266) with [CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_D3D12_CIG_SUPPORTED](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggae12b8a782bebe21b1ac0091bf9f4e2a3a80194e4d9d3af41f1cc828eb54a99f1d). `sharedData` is a ID3D12CommandQueue handle. Support for Vulkan graphics client can be determined using [cuDeviceGetAttribute()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__DEVICE.html#group__cuda__device_1ga9c3e1414f0ad901d3278a4d6645fc266) with [CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_VULKAN_CIG_SUPPORTED](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggae12b8a782bebe21b1ac0091bf9f4e2a3aa3bed53361d118f632efe4776fc90cd3). `sharedData` is a Nvidia specific data blob populated by calling vkGetExternalComputeQueueDataNV(). `execAffinityParams` and `cigParams` are mutually exclusive and cannot both be non-NULL. Setting both to non-NULL values will result in undefined behavior. If both `execAffinityParams` and `cigParams` are NULL, the context will be created as a regular CUDA context.

The three LSBs of the `flags` parameter can be used to control how the OS thread, which owns the CUDA context at the time of an API call, interacts with the OS scheduler when waiting for results from the GPU. Only one of the scheduling flags can be set when creating a context.

Context creation will fail with [CUDA_ERROR_UNKNOWN](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggac6c391505e117393cc2558fff6bfc2e9ac5a6ab0245179d297f1fa56ed0097183) if the compute mode of the device is [CU_COMPUTEMODE_PROHIBITED](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1gga637aab2eadb52e1c1c048b8bad9592d1adb8a226241187db3b1f41999bb70eb47). The function [cuDeviceGetAttribute()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__DEVICE.html#group__cuda__device_1ga9c3e1414f0ad901d3278a4d6645fc266) can be used with [CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_COMPUTE_MODE](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggae12b8a782bebe21b1ac0091bf9f4e2a3af6669a29a6d42968047747cbfc501289) to determine the compute mode of the device. The *nvidia-smi* tool can be used to set the compute mode for \* devices. Documentation for *nvidia-smi* can be obtained by passing a -h option to it.

Context creation will fail with [CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_VALUE](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggac6c391505e117393cc2558fff6bfc2e9a90696c86fcee1f536a1ec7d25867feeb) if invalid parameter was passed by client to create the CUDA context.

Context creation in CIG mode will fail with [CUDA_ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggac6c391505e117393cc2558fff6bfc2e9a54756ae7ade0dfd09faeccb513dd831b) if CIG is not supported by the device or the driver.

pctx.doc: Returned context handle of the new context.

ctxCreateParams.doc: Context creation parameters. Can be NULL to create a regular CUDA context. See [CUctxCreateParams](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/structCUctxCreateParams.html#structcuctxcreateparams) for details.

flags.doc: Context creation flags.

dev.doc: Device to create context on.

cuCtxDestroy.doc:
Destroy a CUDA context.

Destroys the CUDA context specified by `ctx`. The context `ctx` will be destroyed regardless of how many threads it is current to. It is the responsibility of the calling function to ensure that no API call issues using `ctx` while cuCtxDestroy() is executing.

Destroys and cleans up all resources associated with the context. It is the caller’s responsibility to ensure that the context or its resources are not accessed or passed in subsequent API calls and doing so will result in undefined behavior. These resources include CUDA types [CUmodule](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ga9e4ef4dcfba4662b2299acb8d049a1ef), [CUfunction](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1gaba6128b948022f495706d93bc2cea9c8), [CUstream](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1gab946c7f02e09efd788a204718015d88a), [CUevent](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ga6d740185cf0953636d4ae37f68d7559b), [CUarray](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1gad550651524a56766b60f10f0e7628042), [CUmipmappedArray](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ga96db856ab3d2940fb694ce4501d9b583), [CUtexObject](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ga65fb6720dea73d56db0b4d4974be052d), [CUsurfObject](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ga4acc685a8412637d05668e30e984e220), [CUtexref](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1gaec1e8eb9dc48ad748765d1fcc020d6b5), [CUsurfref](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ga7b99472b414f10b2c04dd2530dc7ea76), [CUgraphicsResource](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1gac0c4e1704647178d9c5ba3be46517dcd), CUlinkState, [CUexternalMemory](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1gac9500ef066876b1186f8a54afff900ba) and [CUexternalSemaphore](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ga0bc360152166a414e50a5167250552b8). These resources also include memory allocations by cuMemAlloc(), cuMemAllocHost(), [cuMemAllocManaged()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__MEM.html#group__cuda__mem_1gab347ded34dc326af404aa02af5388a32) and cuMemAllocPitch().

If `ctx` is current to the calling thread then `ctx` will also be popped from the current thread’s context stack (as though cuCtxPopCurrent() were called). If `ctx` is current to other threads, then `ctx` will remain current to those threads, and attempting to access `ctx` from those threads will result in the error [CUDA_ERROR_CONTEXT_IS_DESTROYED](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggac6c391505e117393cc2558fff6bfc2e9ab27ac43f7ce8446f5c9636dd73fb2139).

cuCtxGetApiVersion.signature: CUresult cuCtxGetApiVersion(CUcontext ctx, unsigned int * version)
cuCtxGetApiVersion.doc:
Gets the context’s API version.

Returns a version number in `version` corresponding to the capabilities of the context (e.g. 3010 or 3020), which library developers can use to direct callers to a specific API version. If `ctx` is NULL, returns the API version used to create the currently bound context.

Note that new API versions are only introduced when context capabilities are changed that break binary compatibility, so the API version and driver version may be different. For example, it is valid for the API version to be 3020 while the driver version is 4020.

cuCtxGetCacheConfig.doc:
Returns the preferred cache configuration for the current context.

On devices where the L1 cache and shared memory use the same hardware resources, this function returns through `pconfig` the preferred cache configuration for the current context. This is only a preference. The driver will use the requested configuration if possible, but it is free to choose a different configuration if required to execute functions.

This will return a `pconfig` of [CU_FUNC_CACHE_PREFER_NONE](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1gga3b9bbcf42528b889e9dbe9cfa2aea3eca47d2f367dc3965c27ff748688229dc22) on devices where the size of the L1 cache and shared memory are fixed.

The supported cache configurations are.

cuCtxGetCurrent.doc:
Returns the CUDA context bound to the calling CPU thread.

Returns in `*pctx` the CUDA context bound to the calling CPU thread. If no context is bound to the calling CPU thread then `*pctx` is set to NULL and [CUDA_SUCCESS](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggac6c391505e117393cc2558fff6bfc2e9aa0eed720f8a87cd1c5fd1c453bc7a03d) is returned.

cuCtxGetDevice.doc:
Returns the device handle for the current context.

Returns in `*device` the handle of the current context’s device.

cuCtxGetDevice_v2.doc:
Returns the device handle for the specified context.

Returns in `*device` the handle of the specified context’s device. If the specified context is NULL, the API will return the current context’s device.

device.doc: Returned device handle for the specified context.

ctx.doc: Context for which to obtain the device.

cuCtxGetExecAffinity.doc:
Returns the execution affinity setting for the current context.

Returns in `*pExecAffinity` the current value of `type`. The supported [CUexecAffinityType](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ga14e6345acf2bda65be91eda77cf03f5c) values are.

cuCtxGetFlags.doc:
Returns the flags for the current context.

Returns in `*flags` the flags of the current context. See cuCtxCreate for flag values.

cuCtxGetId.signature: CUresult cuCtxGetId(CUcontext ctx, unsigned long long * ctxId)
cuCtxGetId.doc:
Returns the unique Id associated with the context supplied.

Returns in `ctxId` the unique Id which is associated with a given context. The Id is unique for the life of the program for this instance of CUDA. If context is supplied as NULL and there is one current, the Id of the current context is returned.

ctx.doc: Context for which to obtain the Id.

ctxId.doc: Pointer to store the Id of the context.

cuCtxGetLimit.doc:
Returns resource limits.

Returns in `*pvalue` the current size of `limit`. The supported [CUlimit](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1gae24c2d4214af24139020f1aecaf32665) values are.

cuCtxGetStreamPriorityRange.doc:
Returns numerical values that correspond to the least and greatest stream priorities.

Returns in `*leastPriority` and `*greatestPriority` the numerical values that correspond to the least and greatest stream priorities respectively. Stream priorities follow a convention where lower numbers imply greater priorities. The range of meaningful stream priorities is given by [`*greatestPriority`, `*leastPriority`]. If the user attempts to create a stream with a priority value that is outside the meaningful range as specified by this API, the priority is automatically clamped down or up to either `*leastPriority` or `*greatestPriority` respectively. See [cuStreamCreateWithPriority](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__STREAM.html#group__cuda__stream_1ga95c1a8c7c3dacb13091692dd9c7f7471) for details on creating a priority stream. A NULL may be passed in for `*leastPriority` or `*greatestPriority` if the value is not desired.

This function will return ‘0’ in both `*leastPriority` and `*greatestPriority` if the current context’s device does not support stream priorities (see [cuDeviceGetAttribute](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__DEVICE.html#group__cuda__device_1ga9c3e1414f0ad901d3278a4d6645fc266)).

leastPriority.doc: Pointer to an int in which the numerical value for least stream priority is returned.

greatestPriority.doc: Pointer to an int in which the numerical value for greatest stream priority is returned.

cuCtxPopCurrent.doc:
Pops the current CUDA context from the current CPU thread.

Pops the current CUDA context from the CPU thread and passes back the old context handle in `*pctx`. That context may then be made current to a different CPU thread by calling cuCtxPushCurrent().

If a context was current to the CPU thread before cuCtxCreate() or cuCtxPushCurrent() was called, this function makes that context current to the CPU thread again.

cuCtxPushCurrent.doc:
Pushes a context on the current CPU thread.

Pushes the given context `ctx` onto the CPU thread’s stack of current contexts. The specified context becomes the CPU thread’s current context, so all CUDA functions that operate on the current context are affected.

The previous current context may be made current again by calling cuCtxDestroy() or cuCtxPopCurrent().

cuCtxRecordEvent.doc:
Records an event.

Captures in `hEvent` all the activities of the context `hCtx` at the time of this call. `hEvent` and `hCtx` must be from the same CUDA context, otherwise [CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_HANDLE](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggac6c391505e117393cc2558fff6bfc2e9a0fd2e63260c6317ba943af0f7e4b8d21) will be returned. Calls such as [cuEventQuery()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__EVENT.html#group__cuda__event_1ga6f0704d755066b0ee705749ae911deef) or [cuCtxWaitEvent()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__CTX.html#group__cuda__ctx_1gacf64e420275a8141b1f12bfce3f478f9) will then examine or wait for completion of the work that was captured. Uses of `hCtx` after this call do not modify `hEvent`. If the context passed to `hCtx` is the primary context, `hEvent` will capture all the activities of the primary context and its green contexts. If the context passed to `hCtx` is a context converted from green context via [cuCtxFromGreenCtx()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__GREEN__CONTEXTS.html#group__cuda__green__contexts_1gaf0779ec72ce1d5d7eb003d7d9b25afcb), `hEvent` will capture only the activities of the green context.

cuCtxResetPersistingL2Cache.doc:
Resets all persisting lines in cache to normal status.

[cuCtxResetPersistingL2Cache](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__CTX.html#group__cuda__ctx_1gab529532b5b1aef808295a6d1d18a0823) Resets all persisting lines in cache to normal status. Takes effect on function return.

cuCtxSetCacheConfig.doc:
Sets the preferred cache configuration for the current context.

On devices where the L1 cache and shared memory use the same hardware resources, this sets through `config` the preferred cache configuration for the current context. This is only a preference. The driver will use the requested configuration if possible, but it is free to choose a different configuration if required to execute the function. Any function preference set via [cuFuncSetCacheConfig()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__EXEC.html#group__cuda__exec_1ga40f8c11e81def95dc0072a375f965681) or [cuKernelSetCacheConfig()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__LIBRARY.html#group__cuda__library_1ga8490476e5d3573c7ede78f29bd8cde51) will be preferred over this context-wide setting. Setting the context-wide cache configuration to [CU_FUNC_CACHE_PREFER_NONE](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1gga3b9bbcf42528b889e9dbe9cfa2aea3eca47d2f367dc3965c27ff748688229dc22) will cause subsequent kernel launches to prefer to not change the cache configuration unless required to launch the kernel.

This setting does nothing on devices where the size of the L1 cache and shared memory are fixed.

Launching a kernel with a different preference than the most recent preference setting may insert a device-side synchronization point.

The supported cache configurations are.

cuCtxSetCurrent.doc:
Binds the specified CUDA context to the calling CPU thread.

Binds the specified CUDA context to the calling CPU thread. If `ctx` is NULL then the CUDA context previously bound to the calling CPU thread is unbound and [CUDA_SUCCESS](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggac6c391505e117393cc2558fff6bfc2e9aa0eed720f8a87cd1c5fd1c453bc7a03d) is returned.

If there exists a CUDA context stack on the calling CPU thread, this will replace the top of that stack with `ctx`. If `ctx` is NULL then this will be equivalent to popping the top of the calling CPU thread’s CUDA context stack (or a no-op if the calling CPU thread’s CUDA context stack is empty).

cuCtxSetFlags.doc:
Sets the flags for the current context.

Sets the flags for the current context overwriting previously set ones. See cuDevicePrimaryCtxSetFlags for flag values.

cuCtxSetLimit.doc:
Set resource limits.

Setting `limit` to `value` is a request by the application to update the current limit maintained by the context. The driver is free to modify the requested value to meet h/w requirements (this could be clamping to minimum or maximum values, rounding up to nearest element size, etc). The application can use [cuCtxGetLimit()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__CTX.html#group__cuda__ctx_1ga9f2d47d1745752aa16da7ed0d111b6a8) to find out exactly what the limit has been set to.

Setting each [CUlimit](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1gae24c2d4214af24139020f1aecaf32665) has its own specific restrictions, so each is discussed here.

cuCtxSynchronize.doc:
Block for the current context’s tasks to complete.

Blocks until the current context has completed all preceding requested tasks. If the current context is the primary context, green contexts that have been created will also be synchronized. [cuCtxSynchronize()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__CTX.html#group__cuda__ctx_1ga7a54725f28d34b8c6299f0c6ca579616) returns an error if one of the preceding tasks failed. If the context was created with the [CU_CTX_SCHED_BLOCKING_SYNC](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1gga9f889e28a45a295b5c8ce13aa05f6cd4a62aebfe6432ade3feb32f1a409027852) flag, the CPU thread will block until the GPU context has finished its work.

cuCtxSynchronize_v2.doc:
Block for the specified context’s tasks to complete.

Blocks until the specified context has completed all preceding requested tasks. If the specified context is the primary context, green contexts that have been created will also be synchronized. The API returns an error if one of the preceding tasks failed.

If the context was created with the [CU_CTX_SCHED_BLOCKING_SYNC](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1gga9f889e28a45a295b5c8ce13aa05f6cd4a62aebfe6432ade3feb32f1a409027852) flag, the CPU thread will block until the GPU context has finished its work.

If the specified context is NULL, the API will operate on the current context.

cuCtxWaitEvent.doc:
Make a context wait on an event.

Makes all future work submitted to context `hCtx` wait for all work captured in `hEvent`. The synchronization will be performed on the device and will not block the calling CPU thread. See [cuCtxRecordEvent()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__CTX.html#group__cuda__ctx_1gaf3ee63561a7a371fa9d4dc0e31f94afd) for details on what is captured by an event. If the context passed to `hCtx` is the primary context, the primary context and its green contexts will wait for `hEvent`. If the context passed to `hCtx` is a context converted from green context via [cuCtxFromGreenCtx()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__GREEN__CONTEXTS.html#group__cuda__green__contexts_1gaf0779ec72ce1d5d7eb003d7d9b25afcb), the green context will wait for `hEvent`.

cuCtxAttach.signature: CUresult cuCtxAttach(CUcontext * pctx, unsigned int flags)
cuCtxAttach.doc:
Increment a context’s usage-count.

Note that

Increments the usage count of the context and passes back a context handle in `*pctx` that must be passed to [cuCtxDetach()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__CTX__DEPRECATED.html#group__cuda__ctx__deprecated_1ga3136efc315abd4c4455e875b9dbb65a1) when the application is done with the context. [cuCtxAttach()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__CTX__DEPRECATED.html#group__cuda__ctx__deprecated_1ga37ec990b2a75ed46f25a48b1a425b4f0) fails if there is no context current to the thread.

Currently, the `flags` parameter must be 0.

pctx.doc: Returned context handle of the current context.

flags.doc: Context attach flags (must be 0).

cuCtxDetach.doc:
Decrement a context’s usage-count.

Note that

Decrements the usage count of the context `ctx`, and destroys the context if the usage count goes to 0. The context must be a handle that was passed back by cuCtxCreate() or [cuCtxAttach()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__CTX__DEPRECATED.html#group__cuda__ctx__deprecated_1ga37ec990b2a75ed46f25a48b1a425b4f0), and must be current to the calling thread.

cuCtxGetSharedMemConfig.doc:
Returns the current shared memory configuration for the current context.

This function will return in `pConfig` the current size of shared memory banks in the current context. On devices with configurable shared memory banks, [cuCtxSetSharedMemConfig](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__CTX__DEPRECATED.html#group__cuda__ctx__deprecated_1ga2574235fa643f8f251bf7bc28fac3692) can be used to change this setting, so that all subsequent kernel launches will by default use the new bank size. When [cuCtxGetSharedMemConfig](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__CTX__DEPRECATED.html#group__cuda__ctx__deprecated_1ga17153a1b8b8c756f7ab8505686a4ad74) is called on devices without configurable shared memory, it will return the fixed bank size of the hardware.

The returned bank configurations can be either.

cuCtxSetSharedMemConfig.doc:
Sets the shared memory configuration for the current context.

On devices with configurable shared memory banks, this function will set the context’s shared memory bank size which is used for subsequent kernel launches.

Changed the shared memory configuration between launches may insert a device side synchronization point between those launches.

Changing the shared memory bank size will not increase shared memory usage or affect occupancy of kernels, but may have major effects on performance. Larger bank sizes will allow for greater potential bandwidth to shared memory, but will change what kinds of accesses to shared memory will result in bank conflicts.

This function will do nothing on devices with fixed shared memory bank size.

The supported bank configurations are.

CUcoredumpSettings.doc: Flags for choosing a coredump attribute to get/set.

cuCoredumpDeregisterCompleteCallback.doc:
Deregister a previously registered coredump complete callback.

This function removes a callback that was registered with [cuCoredumpRegisterCompleteCallback](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__COREDUMP.html#group__cuda__coredump_1ga2ccc1cc9d01135950fcc9c2a8ec6f9b5). The callback handle becomes invalid after this call.

cuCoredumpDeregisterStartCallback.doc:
Deregister a previously registered coredump start callback.

This function removes a callback that was registered with [cuCoredumpRegisterStartCallback](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__COREDUMP.html#group__cuda__coredump_1gaff8a2e3192675a2a5b15db50125d04fc). The callback handle becomes invalid after this call.

cuCoredumpGetAttribute.signature: CUresult cuCoredumpGetAttribute(CUcoredumpSettings attrib, void * value, size_t * size)
cuCoredumpGetAttribute.doc:
Allows caller to fetch a coredump attribute value for the current context.

Returns in `*value` the requested value specified by `attrib`. It is up to the caller to ensure that the data type and size of `*value` matches the request.

If the caller calls this function with `*value` equal to NULL, the size of the memory region (in bytes) expected for `attrib` will be placed in `size`.

The supported attributes are.

attrib.doc: The enum defining which value to fetch.

size.doc: The size of the memory region `value` points to.

cuCoredumpGetAttributeGlobal.signature: CUresult cuCoredumpGetAttributeGlobal(CUcoredumpSettings attrib, void * value, size_t * size)
cuCoredumpGetAttributeGlobal.doc:
Allows caller to fetch a coredump attribute value for the entire application.

Returns in `*value` the requested value specified by `attrib`. It is up to the caller to ensure that the data type and size of `*value` matches the request.

If the caller calls this function with `*value` equal to NULL, the size of the memory region (in bytes) expected for `attrib` will be placed in `size`.

The supported attributes are.

attrib.doc: The enum defining which value to fetch.

size.doc: The size of the memory region `value` points to.

cuCoredumpRegisterCompleteCallback.signature: CUresult cuCoredumpRegisterCompleteCallback(CUcoredumpStatusCallback callback, void * userData, CUcoredumpCallbackHandle * callbackOut)
cuCoredumpRegisterCompleteCallback.doc:
Register a callback to be invoked when a GPU coredump completes.

This function registers a callback that will be called when a GPU coredump has been fully collected and written to disk. Callbacks are executed in the order they were registered. The same callback function can be registered multiple times with different userData, and each registration will receive a unique handle.

userData.doc: User data pointer to pass to the callback.

callbackOut.doc: Location to store the callback handle (optional, may be NULL).

cuCoredumpRegisterStartCallback.signature: CUresult cuCoredumpRegisterStartCallback(CUcoredumpStatusCallback callback, void * userData, CUcoredumpCallbackHandle * callbackOut)
cuCoredumpRegisterStartCallback.doc:
Register a callback to be invoked when a GPU coredump begins.

This function registers a callback that will be called when a GPU coredump is initiated, before any coredump data is collected. Callbacks are executed in the order they were registered. The same callback function can be registered multiple times with different userData, and each registration will receive a unique handle.

userData.doc: User data pointer to pass to the callback.

callbackOut.doc: Location to store the callback handle (optional, may be NULL).

cuCoredumpSetAttribute.signature: CUresult cuCoredumpSetAttribute(CUcoredumpSettings attrib, void * value, size_t * size)
cuCoredumpSetAttribute.doc:
Allows caller to set a coredump attribute value for the current context.

This function should be considered an alternate interface to the CUDA-GDB environment variables defined in this document: <https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-gdb/index.html#gpu-coredump>

An important design decision to note is that any coredump environment variable values set before CUDA initializes will take permanent precedence over any values set with this function. This decision was made to ensure no change in behavior for any users that may be currently using these variables to get coredumps.

`*value` shall contain the requested value specified by `set`. It is up to the caller to ensure that the data type and size of `*value` matches the request.

If the caller calls this function with `*value` equal to NULL, the size of the memory region (in bytes) expected for `set` will be placed in `size`.

/note This function will return [CUDA_ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggac6c391505e117393cc2558fff6bfc2e9a54756ae7ade0dfd09faeccb513dd831b) if the caller attempts to set [`CUcoredumpSettings::CU_COREDUMP_ENABLE_ON_EXCEPTION`] on a GPU of with Compute Capability < 6.0. [cuCoredumpSetAttributeGlobal](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__COREDUMP.html#group__cuda__coredump_1gaa7645a8f68dd5379a03852b462727990) works on those platforms as an alternative.

/note [`CUcoredumpSettings::CU_COREDUMP_ENABLE_USER_TRIGGER`] and [`CUcoredumpSettings::CU_COREDUMP_PIPE`] cannot be set on a per-context basis.

The supported attributes are.

attrib.doc: The enum defining which value to set.

size.doc: The size of the memory region `value` points to.

cuCoredumpSetAttributeGlobal.signature: CUresult cuCoredumpSetAttributeGlobal(CUcoredumpSettings attrib, void * value, size_t * size)
cuCoredumpSetAttributeGlobal.doc:
Allows caller to set a coredump attribute value globally.

This function should be considered an alternate interface to the CUDA-GDB environment variables defined in this document: <https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-gdb/index.html#gpu-coredump>

An important design decision to note is that any coredump environment variable values set before CUDA initializes will take permanent precedence over any values set with this function. This decision was made to ensure no change in behavior for any users that may be currently using these variables to get coredumps.

`*value` shall contain the requested value specified by `set`. It is up to the caller to ensure that the data type and size of `*value` matches the request.

If the caller calls this function with `*value` equal to NULL, the size of the memory region (in bytes) expected for `set` will be placed in `size`.

The supported attributes are.

attrib.doc: The enum defining which value to set.

size.doc: The size of the memory region `value` points to.

CUcoredumpCallbackHandle.doc:
Opaque handle representing a registered coredump status callback.

This handle is returned when registering a callback and must be provided when deregistering the callback.

CUcoredumpStatusCallback.signature: typedef void(*CUcoredumpStatusCallback)(void * userData, int pid, CUdevice dev)
CUcoredumpStatusCallback.doc:
Callback function prototype for GPU coredump status notifications.

This callback will be invoked when a GPU coredump begins or completes, depending on which registration function was used. The callback executes synchronously during the coredump process.

fields.Param userData: - User-provided data pointer that was passed during registration
fields.Param pid: - Process ID of the faulted process
fields.Param dev: - Device ordinal where the coredump occurred

CUDA_ARRAY3D_COLOR_ATTACHMENT.doc: This flag indicates that the CUDA array may be bound as a color target in an external graphics API.

CUDA_ARRAY3D_CUBEMAP.doc:
If set, the CUDA array is a collection of six 2D arrays, representing faces of a cube.

The width of such a CUDA array must be equal to its height, and Depth must be six. If [CUDA_ARRAY3D_LAYERED](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1gae4adf555c51852623a3dea962ab8ee85) flag is also set, then the CUDA array is a collection of cubemaps and Depth must be a multiple of six.

CUDA_ARRAY3D_DEFERRED_MAPPING.doc: This flag if set indicates that the CUDA array or CUDA mipmapped array will allow deferred memory mapping.

CUDA_ARRAY3D_DEPTH_TEXTURE.doc: This flag if set indicates that the CUDA array is a DEPTH_TEXTURE.

CUDA_ARRAY3D_LAYERED.doc: If set, the CUDA array is a collection of layers, where each layer is either a 1D or a 2D array and the Depth member of CUDA_ARRAY3D_DESCRIPTOR specifies the number of layers, not the depth of a 3D array.

CUDA_ARRAY3D_SPARSE.doc: This flag if set indicates that the CUDA array or CUDA mipmapped array is a sparse CUDA array or CUDA mipmapped array respectively.

CUDA_ARRAY3D_SURFACE_LDST.doc: This flag must be set in order to bind a surface reference to the CUDA array.

CUDA_ARRAY3D_TEXTURE_GATHER.doc: This flag must be set in order to perform texture gather operations on a CUDA array.

CUDA_ARRAY3D_VIDEO_ENCODE_DECODE.doc: This flag indicates that the CUDA array will be used for hardware accelerated video encode/decode operations.

CUDA_COOPERATIVE_LAUNCH_MULTI_DEVICE_NO_.doc: If set, any subsequent work pushed in a stream that participated in a call to [cuLaunchCooperativeKernelMultiDevice](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__EXEC__DEPRECATED.html#group__cuda__exec__deprecated_1gac4ae8a24130e1e7938514f7e28c76bad) will only wait for the kernel launched on the GPU corresponding to that stream to complete before it begins execution.

If set, each kernel launched as part of [cuLaunchCooperativeKernelMultiDevice](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__EXEC__DEPRECATED.html#group__cuda__exec__deprecated_1gac4ae8a24130e1e7938514f7e28c76bad) only waits for prior work in the stream corresponding to that GPU to complete before the kernel begins execution.

CUDA_EGL_INFINITE_TIMEOUT.doc: Indicates that timeout for [cuEGLStreamConsumerAcquireFrame](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__EGL.html#group__cuda__egl_1ga10507a0acb74a90136caacb363a3c6a7) is infinite.

CUDA_EXTERNAL_MEMORY_DEDICATED.doc: Indicates that the external memory object is a dedicated resource.

CUDA_EXTERNAL_SEMAPHORE_SIGNAL_SKIP_NVSC.doc: When the `flags` parameter of CUDA_EXTERNAL_SEMAPHORE_SIGNAL_PARAMS contains this flag, it indicates that signaling an external semaphore object should skip performing appropriate memory synchronization operations over all the external memory objects that are imported as [CU_EXTERNAL_MEMORY_HANDLE_TYPE_NVSCIBUF](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggabca0bdde9a33c47058b5c97f21e2edd8aadf93206205d155aed8228f4a118d6ee), which otherwise are performed by default to ensure data coherency with other importers of the same NvSciBuf memory objects.

CUDA_EXTERNAL_SEMAPHORE_WAIT_SKIP_NVSCIB.doc: When the `flags` parameter of CUDA_EXTERNAL_SEMAPHORE_WAIT_PARAMS contains this flag, it indicates that waiting on an external semaphore object should skip performing appropriate memory synchronization operations over all the external memory objects that are imported as [CU_EXTERNAL_MEMORY_HANDLE_TYPE_NVSCIBUF](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggabca0bdde9a33c47058b5c97f21e2edd8aadf93206205d155aed8228f4a118d6ee), which otherwise are performed by default to ensure data coherency with other importers of the same NvSciBuf memory objects.

CUDA_NVSCISYNC_ATTR_SIGNAL.doc: When `flags` of [cuDeviceGetNvSciSyncAttributes](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__DEVICE.html#group__cuda__device_1ga0991e2b2b3cedee1ca77d6376e581335) is set to this, it indicates that application needs signaler specific NvSciSyncAttr to be filled by [cuDeviceGetNvSciSyncAttributes](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__DEVICE.html#group__cuda__device_1ga0991e2b2b3cedee1ca77d6376e581335).

CUDA_NVSCISYNC_ATTR_WAIT.doc: When `flags` of [cuDeviceGetNvSciSyncAttributes](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__DEVICE.html#group__cuda__device_1ga0991e2b2b3cedee1ca77d6376e581335) is set to this, it indicates that application needs waiter specific NvSciSyncAttr to be filled by [cuDeviceGetNvSciSyncAttributes](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__DEVICE.html#group__cuda__device_1ga0991e2b2b3cedee1ca77d6376e581335).

CU_ARRAY_SPARSE_PROPERTIES_SINGLE_MIPTAI.doc: Indicates that the layered sparse CUDA array or CUDA mipmapped array has a single mip tail region for all layers.

CU_DEVICE_INVALID.doc: Device that represents an invalid device.

CU_GRAPH_COND_ASSIGN_DEFAULT.doc:
Conditional node handle flags.

Default value is applied when graph is launched.

CU_GRAPH_KERNEL_NODE_PORT_DEFAULT.doc: This port activates when the kernel has finished executing.

CU_GRAPH_KERNEL_NODE_PORT_LAUNCH_ORDER.doc:
This port activates when all blocks of the kernel have begun execution.

See also [CU_LAUNCH_ATTRIBUTE_LAUNCH_COMPLETION_EVENT](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1gga6f6565b334be6bb3134868e10bbdd331a21248c3419121151076d819052270513).

CU_GRAPH_KERNEL_NODE_PORT_PROGRAMMATIC.doc:
This port activates when all blocks of the kernel have performed cudaTriggerProgrammaticLaunchCompletion() or have terminated.

It must be used with edge type [CU_GRAPH_DEPENDENCY_TYPE_PROGRAMMATIC](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1gga4ce440cd353e7761fbf7de1ec963c0b2aaa68c8a335b9f623a1004bfc98cf0e2b). See also [CU_LAUNCH_ATTRIBUTE_PROGRAMMATIC_EVENT](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1gga6f6565b334be6bb3134868e10bbdd331a1667102e857f5d37bb4f460c530dfb13).

CU_LAUNCH_KERNEL_REQUIRED_BLOCK_DIM.doc: Launch with the required block dimension.

CU_LAUNCH_PARAM_BUFFER_POINTER.doc:
Indicator that the next value in the `extra` parameter to [cuLaunchKernel](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__EXEC.html#group__cuda__exec_1gab8f3dc3031b40da29d5f9a7139e52e15) will be a pointer to a buffer containing all kernel parameters used for launching kernel `f`.

This buffer needs to honor all alignment/padding requirements of the individual parameters. If [CU_LAUNCH_PARAM_BUFFER_SIZE](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1gaf339c057cd94562ead93a192e11c17e9) is not also specified in the `extra` array, then [CU_LAUNCH_PARAM_BUFFER_POINTER](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ga36d10d0b40c51372877578a2cffd6acd) will have no effect.

CU_LAUNCH_PARAM_BUFFER_POINTER_AS_INT.doc: C++ compile time constant for CU_LAUNCH_PARAM_BUFFER_POINTER.

CU_LAUNCH_PARAM_BUFFER_SIZE.doc:
Indicator that the next value in the `extra` parameter to [cuLaunchKernel](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__EXEC.html#group__cuda__exec_1gab8f3dc3031b40da29d5f9a7139e52e15) will be a pointer to a size_t which contains the size of the buffer specified with [CU_LAUNCH_PARAM_BUFFER_POINTER](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ga36d10d0b40c51372877578a2cffd6acd).

It is required that [CU_LAUNCH_PARAM_BUFFER_POINTER](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ga36d10d0b40c51372877578a2cffd6acd) also be specified in the `extra` array if the value associated with [CU_LAUNCH_PARAM_BUFFER_SIZE](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1gaf339c057cd94562ead93a192e11c17e9) is not zero.

CU_LAUNCH_PARAM_BUFFER_SIZE_AS_INT.doc: C++ compile time constant for CU_LAUNCH_PARAM_BUFFER_SIZE.

CU_LAUNCH_PARAM_END.doc: End of array terminator for the `extra` parameter to [cuLaunchKernel](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__EXEC.html#group__cuda__exec_1gab8f3dc3031b40da29d5f9a7139e52e15).

CU_LAUNCH_PARAM_END_AS_INT.doc: C++ compile time constant for CU_LAUNCH_PARAM_END.

CU_MEMHOSTALLOC_DEVICEMAP.doc:
If set, host memory is mapped into CUDA address space and cuMemHostGetDevicePointer() may be called on the host pointer.

Flag for [cuMemHostAlloc()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__MEM.html#group__cuda__mem_1ga572ca4011bfcb25034888a14d4e035b9).

CU_MEMHOSTALLOC_PORTABLE.doc:
If set, host memory is portable between CUDA contexts.

Flag for [cuMemHostAlloc()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__MEM.html#group__cuda__mem_1ga572ca4011bfcb25034888a14d4e035b9).

CU_MEMHOSTALLOC_WRITECOMBINED.doc:
If set, host memory is allocated as write-combined - fast to write, faster to DMA, slow to read except via SSE4 streaming load instruction (MOVNTDQA).

Flag for [cuMemHostAlloc()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__MEM.html#group__cuda__mem_1ga572ca4011bfcb25034888a14d4e035b9).

CU_MEMHOSTREGISTER_DEVICEMAP.doc:
If set, host memory is mapped into CUDA address space and cuMemHostGetDevicePointer() may be called on the host pointer.

Flag for cuMemHostRegister().

CU_MEMHOSTREGISTER_IOMEMORY.doc:
If set, the passed memory pointer is treated as pointing to some memory-mapped I/O space, e.g.

belonging to a third-party PCIe device. On Windows the flag is a no-op. On Linux that memory is marked as non cache-coherent for the GPU and is expected to be physically contiguous. It may return [CUDA_ERROR_NOT_PERMITTED](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggac6c391505e117393cc2558fff6bfc2e9ae23d0197c490ec332a43e55b167968a3) if run as an unprivileged user, [CUDA_ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggac6c391505e117393cc2558fff6bfc2e9a54756ae7ade0dfd09faeccb513dd831b) on older Linux kernel versions. On all other platforms, it is not supported and [CUDA_ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggac6c391505e117393cc2558fff6bfc2e9a54756ae7ade0dfd09faeccb513dd831b) is returned. Flag for cuMemHostRegister().

CU_MEMHOSTREGISTER_PORTABLE.doc:
If set, host memory is portable between CUDA contexts.

Flag for cuMemHostRegister().

CU_MEMHOSTREGISTER_READ_ONLY.doc:
If set, the passed memory pointer is treated as pointing to memory that is considered read-only by the device.

On platforms without [CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_PAGEABLE_MEMORY_ACCESS_USES_HOST_PAGE_TABLES](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggae12b8a782bebe21b1ac0091bf9f4e2a3a52c58d6fd1d3a72673cce199ab30cd40), this flag is required in order to register memory mapped to the CPU as read-only. Support for the use of this flag can be queried from the device attribute [CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_READ_ONLY_HOST_REGISTER_SUPPORTED](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggae12b8a782bebe21b1ac0091bf9f4e2a3a3a3a9091a7991536d507dd5eff146d2b). Using this flag with a current context associated with a device that does not have this attribute set will cause cuMemHostRegister to error with [CUDA_ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggac6c391505e117393cc2558fff6bfc2e9a54756ae7ade0dfd09faeccb513dd831b).

CU_MEM_CREATE_USAGE_GPU_DIRECT_RDMA_OVER.doc:
Setting this flag forces GPUDirect RDMA on a locality-domain-localized allocation to use the PCIe (BAR1) path, allowing the allocation to remain locality-domain localized on platforms where the platform-coherent RDMA path does not support localized allocations.

Because on some platforms the PCIe bandwidth is limited, using this flag may result in lower RDMA bandwidth than the default RDMA mapping link. Note that this flag does not itself force PCIe to be used, and that this must be done when creating the RDMA export. [CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_GPU_DIRECT_RDMA_WITH_LOCALIZED_MEMORY_SUPPORTED](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggae12b8a782bebe21b1ac0091bf9f4e2a3a023effd8d7e9dab8196203358adda764) indicates whether this flag is needed to create GPUDirect RDMA capable localized memory allocations. This flag is only valid if gpuDirectRDMACapable is set.

CU_MEM_CREATE_USAGE_HW_DECOMPRESS.doc: This flag, if set, indicates that the memory will be used as a buffer for hardware accelerated decompression.

CU_MEM_CREATE_USAGE_TILE_POOL.doc: This flag if set indicates that the memory will be used as a tile pool.

CU_MEM_POOL_CREATE_USAGE_HW_DECOMPRESS.doc: This flag, if set, indicates that the memory will be used as a buffer for hardware accelerated decompression.

CU_PARAM_TR_DEFAULT.doc: For texture references loaded into the module, use default texunit from texture reference.

CU_STREAM_LEGACY.doc:
Legacy stream handle.

Stream handle that can be passed as a CUstream to use an implicit stream with legacy synchronization behavior.

See details of the.

CU_STREAM_PER_THREAD.doc:
Per-thread stream handle.

Stream handle that can be passed as a CUstream to use an implicit stream with per-thread synchronization behavior.

See details of the.

CU_TRSA_OVERRIDE_FORMAT.doc:
Override the texref format with a format inferred from the array.

Flag for [cuTexRefSetArray()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TEXREF__DEPRECATED.html#group__cuda__texref__deprecated_1ga34435b306682531716243239f0084fed).

CU_TRSF_DISABLE_TRILINEAR_OPTIMIZATION.doc:
Disable any trilinear filtering optimizations.

Flag for [cuTexRefSetFlags()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TEXREF__DEPRECATED.html#group__cuda__texref__deprecated_1ga554ffd896487533c36810f2e45bb7a28) and [cuTexObjectCreate()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TEXOBJECT.html#group__cuda__texobject_1ga1f6dd0f9cbf56db725b1f45aa0a7218a).

CU_TRSF_NORMALIZED_COORDINATES.doc:
Use normalized texture coordinates in the range [0,1) instead of [0,dim).

Flag for [cuTexRefSetFlags()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TEXREF__DEPRECATED.html#group__cuda__texref__deprecated_1ga554ffd896487533c36810f2e45bb7a28) and [cuTexObjectCreate()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TEXOBJECT.html#group__cuda__texobject_1ga1f6dd0f9cbf56db725b1f45aa0a7218a).

CU_TRSF_READ_AS_INTEGER.doc:
Read the texture as integers rather than promoting the values to floats in the range [0,1].

Flag for [cuTexRefSetFlags()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TEXREF__DEPRECATED.html#group__cuda__texref__deprecated_1ga554ffd896487533c36810f2e45bb7a28) and [cuTexObjectCreate()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TEXOBJECT.html#group__cuda__texobject_1ga1f6dd0f9cbf56db725b1f45aa0a7218a).

CU_TRSF_SEAMLESS_CUBEMAP.doc:
Enable seamless cube map filtering.

Flag for [cuTexObjectCreate()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TEXOBJECT.html#group__cuda__texobject_1ga1f6dd0f9cbf56db725b1f45aa0a7218a).

CU_TRSF_SRGB.doc:
Perform sRGB->linear conversion during texture read.

Flag for [cuTexRefSetFlags()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TEXREF__DEPRECATED.html#group__cuda__texref__deprecated_1ga554ffd896487533c36810f2e45bb7a28) and [cuTexObjectCreate()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TEXOBJECT.html#group__cuda__texobject_1ga1f6dd0f9cbf56db725b1f45aa0a7218a).

MAX_PLANES.doc: Maximum number of planes per frame.

CUDA_POINTER_ATTRIBUTE_ACCESS_FLAGS.doc: Access flags that specify the level of access the current context’s device has on the memory referenced.

CU_POINTER_ATTRIBUTE_ACCESS_FLAG_NONE.doc: No access, meaning the device cannot access this memory at all, thus must be staged through accessible memory in order to complete certain operations.

CU_POINTER_ATTRIBUTE_ACCESS_FLAG_READ.doc: Read-only access, meaning writes to this memory are considered invalid accesses and thus return error in that case.

CU_POINTER_ATTRIBUTE_ACCESS_FLAG_READWRI.doc: Read-write access, the device has full read-write access to the memory.

CUGPUDirectRDMAWritesOrdering.doc: Platform native ordering for GPUDirect RDMA writes.

CU_GPU_DIRECT_RDMA_WRITES_ORDERING_NONE.doc:
The device does not natively support ordering of remote writes.

[cuFlushGPUDirectRDMAWrites()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__DEVICE.html#group__cuda__device_1ga265e3c82ef0f0fe035f85c4c45a8fbdf) can be leveraged if supported.

CU_GPU_DIRECT_RDMA_WRITES_ORDERING_OWNER.doc: Natively, the device can consistently consume remote writes, although other CUDA devices may not.

CU_GPU_DIRECT_RDMA_WRITES_ORDERING_ALL_D.doc: Any CUDA device in the system can consistently consume remote writes to this device.

CUaccessProperty.doc: Specifies performance hint with [CUaccessPolicyWindow](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ga1838e6438f39944217e384bf2adad477) for hitProp and missProp members.

CU_ACCESS_PROPERTY_STREAMING.doc: Streaming access is less likely to persit from cache.

CU_ACCESS_PROPERTY_PERSISTING.doc: Persisting access is more likely to persist in cache.

CU_AD_FORMAT_BC1_UNORM.doc: 4 channel unsigned normalized block-compressed (BC1 compression) format.

CU_AD_FORMAT_BC1_UNORM_SRGB.doc: 4 channel unsigned normalized block-compressed (BC1 compression) format with sRGB encoding.

CU_AD_FORMAT_BC2_UNORM.doc: 4 channel unsigned normalized block-compressed (BC2 compression) format.

CU_AD_FORMAT_BC2_UNORM_SRGB.doc: 4 channel unsigned normalized block-compressed (BC2 compression) format with sRGB encoding.

CU_AD_FORMAT_BC3_UNORM.doc: 4 channel unsigned normalized block-compressed (BC3 compression) format.

CU_AD_FORMAT_BC3_UNORM_SRGB.doc: 4 channel unsigned normalized block-compressed (BC3 compression) format with sRGB encoding.

CU_AD_FORMAT_BC4_UNORM.doc: 1 channel unsigned normalized block-compressed (BC4 compression) format.

CU_AD_FORMAT_BC4_SNORM.doc: 1 channel signed normalized block-compressed (BC4 compression) format.

CU_AD_FORMAT_BC5_UNORM.doc: 2 channel unsigned normalized block-compressed (BC5 compression) format.

CU_AD_FORMAT_BC5_SNORM.doc: 2 channel signed normalized block-compressed (BC5 compression) format.

CU_AD_FORMAT_BC6H_UF16.doc: 3 channel unsigned half-float block-compressed (BC6H compression) format.

CU_AD_FORMAT_BC6H_SF16.doc: 3 channel signed half-float block-compressed (BC6H compression) format.

CU_AD_FORMAT_BC7_UNORM.doc: 4 channel unsigned normalized block-compressed (BC7 compression) format.

CU_AD_FORMAT_BC7_UNORM_SRGB.doc: 4 channel unsigned normalized block-compressed (BC7 compression) format with sRGB encoding.

CU_AD_FORMAT_YUY2.doc: 2 channel, 8-bit YUV packed planar format, with 4:2:2 sampling.

CU_AD_FORMAT_Y210.doc: 2 channel, 10-bit YUV packed planar format, with 4:2:2 sampling.

CU_AD_FORMAT_Y216.doc: 2 channel, 16-bit YUV packed planar format, with 4:2:2 sampling.

CU_AD_FORMAT_AYUV.doc: 4 channel, 8-bit YUV packed planar format, with 4:4:4 sampling.

CU_AD_FORMAT_Y410.doc: 10-bit YUV packed planar format, with 4:4:4 sampling.

CU_AD_FORMAT_Y416.doc: 4 channel, 12-bit YUV packed planar format, with 4:4:4 sampling.

CU_AD_FORMAT_Y444_PLANAR8.doc: 3 channel 8-bit YUV planar format, with 4:4:4 sampling.

CU_AD_FORMAT_Y444_PLANAR10.doc: 3 channel 10-bit YUV planar format, with 4:4:4 sampling.

CU_AD_FORMAT_YUV444_8bit_SemiPlanar.doc: 3 channel 8-bit YUV semi-planar format, with 4:4:4 sampling.

CU_AD_FORMAT_YUV444_16bit_SemiPlanar.doc: 3 channel 16-bit YUV semi-planar format, with 4:4:4 sampling.

CU_AD_FORMAT_UINT8_PACKED_422.doc: 4 channel unsigned 8-bit YUV packed format, with 4:2:2 sampling.

CU_AD_FORMAT_UINT8_PACKED_444.doc: 4 channel unsigned 8-bit YUV packed format, with 4:4:4 sampling.

CU_AD_FORMAT_UINT8_SEMIPLANAR_420.doc: 3 channel unsigned 8-bit YUV semi-planar format, with 4:2:0 sampling.

CU_AD_FORMAT_UINT16_SEMIPLANAR_420.doc: 3 channel unsigned 16-bit YUV semi-planar format, with 4:2:0 sampling.

CU_AD_FORMAT_UINT8_SEMIPLANAR_422.doc: 3 channel unsigned 8-bit YUV semi-planar format, with 4:2:2 sampling.

CU_AD_FORMAT_UINT16_SEMIPLANAR_422.doc: 3 channel unsigned 16-bit YUV semi-planar format, with 4:2:2 sampling.

CU_AD_FORMAT_UINT8_SEMIPLANAR_444.doc: 3 channel unsigned 8-bit YUV semi-planar format, with 4:4:4 sampling.

CU_AD_FORMAT_UINT16_SEMIPLANAR_444.doc: 3 channel unsigned 16-bit YUV semi-planar format, with 4:4:4 sampling.

CU_AD_FORMAT_UINT8_PLANAR_420.doc: 3 channel unsigned 8-bit YUV planar format, with 4:2:0 sampling.

CU_AD_FORMAT_UINT16_PLANAR_420.doc: 3 channel unsigned 16-bit YUV planar format, with 4:2:0 sampling.

CU_AD_FORMAT_UINT8_PLANAR_422.doc: 3 channel unsigned 8-bit YUV planar format, with 4:2:2 sampling.

CU_AD_FORMAT_UINT16_PLANAR_422.doc: 3 channel unsigned 16-bit YUV planar format, with 4:2:2 sampling.

CU_AD_FORMAT_UINT8_PLANAR_444.doc: 3 channel unsigned 8-bit YUV planar format, with 4:4:4 sampling.

CU_AD_FORMAT_UINT16_PLANAR_444.doc: 3 channel unsigned 16-bit YUV planar format, with 4:4:4 sampling.

CUasyncNotificationType.doc: Types of async notification that can be sent.

CU_ASYNC_NOTIFICATION_TYPE_OVER_BUDGET.doc: Sent when the process has exceeded its device memory budget.

CIG_DATA_TYPE_NV_BLOB.doc: Nvidia specific data blob used for Vulkan and other NV clients.

CUclusterSchedulingPolicy.doc:
Cluster scheduling policies.

These may be passed to [cuFuncSetAttribute](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__EXEC.html#group__cuda__exec_1ga0e37dce0173bc883aa1e5b14dd747f26) or [cuKernelSetAttribute](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__LIBRARY.html#group__cuda__library_1ga1093ade718915249de3b14320d567067).

CU_CLUSTER_SCHEDULING_POLICY_SPREAD.doc: spread the blocks within a cluster to the SMs.

CU_CLUSTER_SCHEDULING_POLICY_LOAD_BALANC.doc: allow the hardware to load-balance the blocks in a cluster to the SMs.

CU_COMPUTEMODE_DEFAULT.doc: Default compute mode (Multiple contexts allowed per device).

CU_COMPUTEMODE_PROHIBITED.doc: Compute-prohibited mode (No contexts can be created on this device at this time).

CU_COMPUTEMODE_EXCLUSIVE_PROCESS.doc: Compute-exclusive-process mode (Only one context used by a single process can be present on this device at a time).

CU_CTX_SCHED_BLOCKING_SYNC.doc: Set blocking synchronization as default scheduling.

CU_CTX_BLOCKING_SYNC.doc: Set blocking synchronization as default scheduling.

CU_CTX_LMEM_RESIZE_TO_MAX.doc: Keep local memory allocation after launch.

CU_CTX_COREDUMP_ENABLE.doc: Trigger coredumps from exceptions in this context.

CU_CTX_USER_COREDUMP_ENABLE.doc: Enable user pipe to trigger coredumps in this context.

CU_CTX_SYNC_MEMOPS.doc: Ensure synchronous memory operations on this context will synchronize.

CU_DEVICE_NUMA_CONFIG_NONE.doc: The GPU is not a NUMA node.

CU_DEVICE_NUMA_CONFIG_NUMA_NODE.doc: The GPU is a NUMA node, [`CUdevice_attribute::CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_NUMA_ID`] contains its NUMA ID.

CU_DEVICE_P2P_ATTRIBUTE_PERFORMANCE_RANK.doc: A relative value indicating the performance of the link between two devices.

CU_DEVICE_P2P_ATTRIBUTE_NATIVE_ATOMIC_SU.doc: All CUDA-valid atomic operation over the link are supported.

CU_DEVICE_P2P_ATTRIBUTE_CUDA_ARRAY_ACCES.doc: Accessing CUDA arrays over the link supported.

CU_DEVICE_P2P_ATTRIBUTE_ONLY_PARTIAL_NAT.doc: Only some CUDA-valid atomic operations over the link are supported.

CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_MAX_THREADS_PER_BLOC.doc: Maximum number of threads per block.

CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_MAX_SHARED_MEMORY_PE.doc: Maximum shared memory available per block in bytes.

CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_TOTAL_CONSTANT_MEMOR.doc: Memory available on device for **constant** variables in a CUDA C kernel in bytes.

CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_MAX_PITCH.doc: Maximum pitch in bytes allowed by memory copies.

CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_MAX_REGISTERS_PER_BL.doc: Maximum number of 32-bit registers available per block.

CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_GPU_OVERLAP.doc:
Device can possibly copy memory and execute a kernel concurrently.

Deprecated. Use instead [`CUdevice_attribute::CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_ASYNC_ENGINE_COUNT`].

CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_KERNEL_EXEC_TIMEOUT.doc: Specifies whether there is a run time limit on kernels.

CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_INTEGRATED.doc: Device is integrated with host memory.

CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_CAN_MAP_HOST_MEMORY.doc: Device can map host memory into CUDA address space.

CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_MAXIMUM_TEXTURE2D_LA.doc: Maximum layers in a 2D layered texture.

CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_CONCURRENT_KERNELS.doc: Device can possibly execute multiple kernels concurrently.

CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_PCI_BUS_ID.doc: PCI bus ID of the device.

CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_PCI_DEVICE_ID.doc: PCI device ID of the device.

CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_TCC_DRIVER.doc: Device is using TCC driver model.

CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_MEMORY_CLOCK_RATE.doc: Peak memory clock frequency in kilohertz.

CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_GLOBAL_MEMORY_BUS_WI.doc: Global memory bus width in bits.

CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_L2_CACHE_SIZE.doc: Size of L2 cache in bytes.

CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_UNIFIED_ADDRESSING.doc: Device shares a unified address space with the host.

CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_MAXIMUM_TEXTURE1D_LA.doc: Maximum layers in a 1D layered texture.

CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_MAXIMUM_TEXTURE2D_GA.doc: Maximum 2D texture width if CUDA_ARRAY3D_TEXTURE_GATHER is set.
Maximum 2D texture height if CUDA_ARRAY3D_TEXTURE_GATHER is set.

CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_PCI_DOMAIN_ID.doc: PCI domain ID of the device.

CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_MAXIMUM_TEXTURECUBEM.doc: Maximum layers in a cubemap layered texture.

CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_MAXIMUM_SURFACE1D_LA.doc: Maximum layers in a 1D layered surface.

CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_MAXIMUM_SURFACE2D_LA.doc: Maximum layers in a 2D layered surface.

CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_MAXIMUM_SURFACECUBEM.doc: Maximum layers in a cubemap layered surface.

CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_MAXIMUM_TEXTURE1D_LI.doc:
do not use.

Use cudaDeviceGetTexture1DLinearMaxWidth() or [cuDeviceGetTexture1DLinearMaxWidth()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__DEVICE.html#group__cuda__device_1gab41b3a675bae9932bffa1c0ae969b1e0) instead.

CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_MAXIMUM_TEXTURE2D_LI.doc: Maximum 2D linear texture pitch in bytes.

CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_GLOBAL_L1_CACHE_SUPP.doc: Device supports caching globals in L1.

CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_LOCAL_L1_CACHE_SUPPO.doc: Device supports caching locals in L1.

CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_MAX_SHARED_MEMORY_PE.doc: Maximum shared memory available per multiprocessor in bytes.

CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_MAX_REGISTERS_PER_MU.doc: Maximum number of 32-bit registers available per multiprocessor.

CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_MANAGED_MEMORY.doc: Device can allocate managed memory on this system.

CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_MULTI_GPU_BOARD.doc: Device is on a multi-GPU board.

CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_MULTI_GPU_BOARD_GROU.doc: Unique id for a group of devices on the same multi-GPU board.

CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_HOST_NATIVE_ATOMIC_S.doc: Link between the device and the host supports all native atomic operations.

CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_SINGLE_TO_DOUBLE_PRE.doc: Ratio of single precision performance (in floating-point operations per second) to double precision performance.

CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_PAGEABLE_MEMORY_ACCE.doc: Device supports coherently accessing pageable memory without calling cudaHostRegister on it.

CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_CONCURRENT_MANAGED_A.doc: Device can coherently access managed memory concurrently with the CPU.

CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_CAN_USE_HOST_POINTER.doc: Device can access host registered memory at the same virtual address as the CPU.

CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_CAN_USE_STREAM_MEM_O.doc: along with v1 MemOps API, cuStreamBatchMemOp and related APIs are supported.

CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_CAN_USE_64_BIT_STREA.doc: along with v1 MemOps API, 64-bit operations are supported in cuStreamBatchMemOp and related APIs.

CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_CAN_USE_STREAM_WAIT_.doc: along with v1 MemOps API, [CU_STREAM_WAIT_VALUE_NOR](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggaf16864e8693d888f8178067470001b21a2f10c357c1882ae7b0b947225c1a0d55) is supported.
