edgeData.doc: Optional array to return edge data for each dependency.

cuGraphNodeGetDependentNodes.signature: CUresult cuGraphNodeGetDependentNodes(CUgraphNode hNode, CUgraphNode * dependentNodes, CUgraphEdgeData * edgeData, size_t * numDependentNodes)
cuGraphNodeGetDependentNodes.doc:
Returns a node’s dependent nodes.

Returns a list of `node's` dependent nodes. `dependentNodes` may be NULL, in which case this function will return the number of dependent nodes in `numDependentNodes`. Otherwise, `numDependentNodes` entries will be filled in. If `numDependentNodes` is higher than the actual number of dependent nodes, the remaining entries in `dependentNodes` will be set to NULL, and the number of nodes actually obtained will be returned in `numDependentNodes`.

Note that if an edge has non-zero (non-default) edge data and `edgeData` is NULL, this API will return [CUDA_ERROR_LOSSY_QUERY](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggac6c391505e117393cc2558fff6bfc2e9a0c2195e65483c3e7f0ccbf52370c33f7). If `edgeData` is non-NULL, then `dependentNodes` must be as well.

hNode.doc: Node to query.

dependentNodes.doc: Pointer to return the dependent nodes.

edgeData.doc: Optional pointer to return edge data for dependent nodes.

cuGraphNodeGetEnabled.signature: CUresult cuGraphNodeGetEnabled(CUgraphExec hGraphExec, CUgraphNode hNode, unsigned int * isEnabled)
cuGraphNodeGetEnabled.doc:
Query whether a node in the given graphExec is enabled.

Sets isEnabled to 1 if `hNode` is enabled, or 0 if `hNode` is disabled.

The node is identified by the corresponding node `hNode` in the non-executable graph, from which the executable graph was instantiated.

`hNode` must not have been removed from the original graph.

hGraphExec.doc: The executable graph in which to set the specified node.

hNode.doc: Node from the graph from which graphExec was instantiated.

isEnabled.doc: Location to return the enabled status of the node.

cuGraphNodeGetLocalId.signature: CUresult cuGraphNodeGetLocalId(CUgraphNode hNode, unsigned int * nodeId)
cuGraphNodeGetLocalId.doc:
Returns the local node id of a given graph node.

Returns the node id of `hNode` in `*nodeId`. The nodeId matches that referenced by [cuGraphDebugDotPrint](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__GRAPH.html#group__cuda__graph_1ga0fb0c4d319477a0a98da005fcb0dacc4). The local nodeId and graphId together can uniquely identify the node.

hNode.doc: Node to query.

cuGraphNodeGetParams.doc:
Return a graph node’s parameters.

Returns the parameters of graph node `hNode` in `*nodeParams`.

Any pointers returned in `*nodeParams` point to driver-owned memory associated with the node. This memory remains valid until the node is destroyed. Any memory pointed to from `*nodeParams` must not be modified.

The returned parameters are a description of the node, but may not be identical to the struct provided at creation and may not be suitable for direct creation of identical nodes. This is because parameters may be partially unspecified and filled in by the driver at creation, may reference non-copyable handles, or may describe ownership semantics or other parameters that govern behavior of node creation but are not part of the final functional descriptor.

hNode.doc: Node to get the parameters for.

cuGraphNodeGetToolsId.signature: CUresult cuGraphNodeGetToolsId(CUgraphNode hNode, unsigned long long * toolsNodeId)
cuGraphNodeGetToolsId.doc: Returns an id used by tools to identify a given node.

hNode.doc: Node to query.

\\*toolsNodeId.doc: Pointer to return the id used by tools.

cuGraphNodeGetType.doc:
Returns a node’s type.

Returns the node type of `hNode` in `type`.

hNode.doc: Node to query.

type.doc: Pointer to return the node type.

cuGraphNodeSetEnabled.signature: CUresult cuGraphNodeSetEnabled(CUgraphExec hGraphExec, CUgraphNode hNode, unsigned int isEnabled)
cuGraphNodeSetEnabled.doc:
Enables or disables the specified node in the given graphExec.

Sets `hNode` to be either enabled or disabled. Disabled nodes are functionally equivalent to empty nodes until they are reenabled. Existing node parameters are not affected by disabling/enabling the node.

The node is identified by the corresponding node `hNode` in the non-executable graph, from which the executable graph was instantiated.

`hNode` must not have been removed from the original graph.

The modifications only affect future launches of `hGraphExec`. Already enqueued or running launches of `hGraphExec` are not affected by this call. `hNode` is also not modified by this call.

If `hNode` is a device-updatable kernel node, the next upload/launch of `hGraphExec` will overwrite any previous device-side updates. Additionally, applying host updates to a device-updatable kernel node while it is being updated from the device will result in undefined behavior.

hGraphExec.doc: The executable graph in which to set the specified node.

hNode.doc: Node from the graph from which graphExec was instantiated.

isEnabled.doc: Node is enabled if != 0, otherwise the node is disabled.

cuGraphNodeSetParams.doc:
Update a graph node’s parameters.

Sets the parameters of graph node `hNode` to `nodeParams`. The node type specified by `nodeParams->type` must match the type of `hNode`. `nodeParams` must be fully initialized and all unused bytes (reserved, padding) zeroed.

Modifying parameters is not supported for node types [`CUgraphNodeType::CU_GRAPH_NODE_TYPE_MEM_ALLOC`] and [`CUgraphNodeType::CU_GRAPH_NODE_TYPE_MEM_FREE`].

hNode.doc: Node to set the parameters for.

cuGraphNodeSetParams_v2.doc:
Update a graph node’s parameters.

Sets the parameters of graph node `hNode` to `nodeParams`. The node type specified by `nodeParams->type` must match the type of `hNode`. `nodeParams` must be fully initialized and all unused bytes (reserved, padding) zeroed.

Modifying parameters is not supported for node types [`CUgraphNodeType::CU_GRAPH_NODE_TYPE_MEM_ALLOC`] and [`CUgraphNodeType::CU_GRAPH_NODE_TYPE_MEM_FREE`].

For kernel nodes, if both the kernel node’s [CUfunction](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1gaba6128b948022f495706d93bc2cea9c8) and ctx are non-NULL, the underlying device context of ctx must match the device context that the [CUfunction](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1gaba6128b948022f495706d93bc2cea9c8) was loaded into; otherwise the call returns [CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_CONTEXT](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggac6c391505e117393cc2558fff6bfc2e9aa484e9af32c1e9893ff21f0e0191a12d).

hNode.doc: Node to set the parameters for.

cuGraphReleaseUserObject.signature: CUresult cuGraphReleaseUserObject(CUgraph graph, CUuserObject object, unsigned int count)
cuGraphReleaseUserObject.doc:
Release a user object reference from a graph.

Releases user object references owned by a graph.

See CUDA User Objects in the CUDA C++ Programming Guide for more information on user objects.

graph.doc: The graph that will release the reference.

object.doc: The user object to release a reference for.

count.doc: The number of references to release, typically 1. Must be nonzero and not larger than INT_MAX.

cuGraphRemoveDependencies.signature: CUresult cuGraphRemoveDependencies(CUgraph hGraph, const CUgraphNode * from, const CUgraphNode * to, const CUgraphEdgeData * edgeData, size_t numDependencies)
cuGraphRemoveDependencies.doc:
Removes dependency edges from a graph.

The number of `dependencies` to be removed is defined by `numDependencies`. Elements in `from` and `to` at corresponding indices define a dependency. Each node in `from` and `to` must belong to `hGraph`.

If `numDependencies` is 0, elements in `from` and `to` will be ignored. Specifying an edge that does not exist in the graph, with data matching `edgeData`, results in an error. `edgeData` is nullable, which is equivalent to passing default (zeroed) data for each edge.

Dependencies cannot be removed from graphs which contain allocation or free nodes. Any attempt to do so will return an error.

hGraph.doc: Graph from which to remove dependencies.

from.doc: Array of nodes that provide the dependencies.

edgeData.doc: Optional array of edge data. If NULL, edge data is assumed to be default (zeroed).

numDependencies.doc: Number of dependencies to be removed.

cuGraphRetainUserObject.signature: CUresult cuGraphRetainUserObject(CUgraph graph, CUuserObject object, unsigned int count, unsigned int flags)
cuGraphRetainUserObject.doc:
Retain a reference to a user object from a graph.

Creates or moves user object references that will be owned by a CUDA graph.

See CUDA User Objects in the CUDA C++ Programming Guide for more information on user objects.

graph.doc: The graph to associate the reference with.

object.doc: The user object to retain a reference for.

count.doc: The number of references to add to the graph, typically 1. Must be nonzero and not larger than INT_MAX.

flags.doc: The optional flag [CU_GRAPH_USER_OBJECT_MOVE](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1gga1649c3055c83c32f812faac63c8da0b1af9b815bff431e87e54037568c4677b9d) transfers references from the calling thread, rather than create new references. Pass 0 to create new references.

cuGraphUpload.doc:
Uploads an executable graph in a stream.

Uploads `hGraphExec` to the device in `hStream` without executing it. Uploads of the same `hGraphExec` will be serialized. Each upload is ordered behind both any previous work in `hStream` and any previous launches of `hGraphExec`. Uses memory cached by `stream` to back the allocations owned by `hGraphExec`.

hStream.doc: Stream in which to upload the graph.

cuUserObjectCreate.signature: CUresult cuUserObjectCreate(CUuserObject * object_out, void * ptr, CUhostFn destroy, unsigned int initialRefcount, unsigned int flags)
cuUserObjectCreate.doc:
Create a user object.

Create a user object with the specified destructor callback and initial reference count. The initial references are owned by the caller.

Destructor callbacks cannot make CUDA API calls and should avoid blocking behavior, as they are executed by a shared internal thread. Another thread may be signaled to perform such actions, if it does not block forward progress of tasks scheduled through CUDA.

See CUDA User Objects in the CUDA C++ Programming Guide for more information on user objects.

object_out.doc: Location to return the user object handle.

ptr.doc: The pointer to pass to the destroy function.

destroy.doc: Callback to free the user object when it is no longer in use.

initialRefcount.doc: The initial refcount to create the object with, typically 1. The initial references are owned by the calling thread.

flags.doc: Currently it is required to pass [CU_USER_OBJECT_NO_DESTRUCTOR_SYNC](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1gga11c53cd19ee840b3b0f597d57451e943a30bb85019bed1f36b8130cef76085e27), which is the only defined flag. This indicates that the destroy callback cannot be waited on by any CUDA API. Users requiring synchronization of the callback should signal its completion manually.

cuUserObjectRelease.signature: CUresult cuUserObjectRelease(CUuserObject object, unsigned int count)
cuUserObjectRelease.doc:
Release a reference to a user object.

Releases user object references owned by the caller. The object’s destructor is invoked if the reference count reaches zero.

It is undefined behavior to release references not owned by the caller, or to use a user object handle after all references are released.

See CUDA User Objects in the CUDA C++ Programming Guide for more information on user objects.

count.doc: The number of references to release, typically 1. Must be nonzero and not larger than INT_MAX.

cuUserObjectRetain.signature: CUresult cuUserObjectRetain(CUuserObject object, unsigned int count)
cuUserObjectRetain.doc:
Retain a reference to a user object.

Retains new references to a user object. The new references are owned by the caller.

See CUDA User Objects in the CUDA C++ Programming Guide for more information on user objects.

count.doc: The number of references to retain, typically 1. Must be nonzero and not larger than INT_MAX.

cuGraphicsMapResources.signature: CUresult cuGraphicsMapResources(unsigned int count, CUgraphicsResource * resources, CUstream hStream)
cuGraphicsMapResources.doc:
Map graphics resources for access by CUDA.

Maps the `count` graphics resources in `resources` for access by CUDA.

The resources in `resources` may be accessed by CUDA until they are unmapped. The graphics API from which `resources` were registered should not access any resources while they are mapped by CUDA. If an application does so, the results are undefined.

This function provides the synchronization guarantee that any graphics calls issued before [cuGraphicsMapResources()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__GRAPHICS.html#group__cuda__graphics_1gaffcfd8e78d82cc4f6dd987e8bce4edb0) will complete before any subsequent CUDA work issued in `stream` begins.

If `resources` includes any duplicate entries then [CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_HANDLE](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggac6c391505e117393cc2558fff6bfc2e9a0fd2e63260c6317ba943af0f7e4b8d21) is returned. If any of `resources` are presently mapped for access by CUDA then [CUDA_ERROR_ALREADY_MAPPED](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggac6c391505e117393cc2558fff6bfc2e9a240bb253a699176d9f49ee2f2c91b61b) is returned.

count.doc: Number of resources to map.

resources.doc: Resources to map for CUDA usage.

cuGraphicsResourceGetMappedMipmappedArra.doc:
Get a mipmapped array through which to access a mapped graphics resource.

Returns in `*pMipmappedArray` a mipmapped array through which the mapped graphics resource `resource`. The value set in `*pMipmappedArray` may change every time that `resource` is mapped.

If `resource` is not a texture then it cannot be accessed via a mipmapped array and [CUDA_ERROR_NOT_MAPPED_AS_ARRAY](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggac6c391505e117393cc2558fff6bfc2e9a037f39ebe1bbd16d1b162f4456d507c5) is returned. If `resource` is not mapped then [CUDA_ERROR_NOT_MAPPED](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggac6c391505e117393cc2558fff6bfc2e9ae098433b926c9afdb6b6bdf191629447) is returned.

pMipmappedArray.doc: Returned mipmapped array through which `resource` may be accessed.

cuGraphicsResourceGetMappedPointer.signature: CUresult cuGraphicsResourceGetMappedPointer(CUdeviceptr * pDevPtr, size_t * pSize, CUgraphicsResource resource)
cuGraphicsResourceGetMappedPointer.doc:
Get a device pointer through which to access a mapped graphics resource.

Returns in `*pDevPtr` a pointer through which the mapped graphics resource `resource` may be accessed. Returns in `pSize` the size of the memory in bytes which may be accessed from that pointer. The value set in `pPointer` may change every time that `resource` is mapped.

If `resource` is not a buffer then it cannot be accessed via a pointer and [CUDA_ERROR_NOT_MAPPED_AS_POINTER](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggac6c391505e117393cc2558fff6bfc2e9aa7ceef277b14abcb140c4ffa72a37473) is returned. If `resource` is not mapped then [CUDA_ERROR_NOT_MAPPED](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggac6c391505e117393cc2558fff6bfc2e9ae098433b926c9afdb6b6bdf191629447) is returned.

pDevPtr.doc: Returned pointer through which `resource` may be accessed.

pSize.doc: Returned size of the buffer accessible starting at `*pPointer`.

cuGraphicsResourceSetMapFlags.doc:
Set usage flags for mapping a graphics resource.

Set `flags` for mapping the graphics resource `resource`.

Changes to `flags` will take effect the next time `resource` is mapped. The `flags` argument may be any of the following:

If `resource` is presently mapped for access by CUDA then [CUDA_ERROR_ALREADY_MAPPED](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggac6c391505e117393cc2558fff6bfc2e9a240bb253a699176d9f49ee2f2c91b61b) is returned. If `flags` is not one of the above values then [CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_VALUE](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggac6c391505e117393cc2558fff6bfc2e9a90696c86fcee1f536a1ec7d25867feeb) is returned.

resource.doc: Registered resource to set flags for.

flags.doc: Parameters for resource mapping.

cuGraphicsSubResourceGetMappedArray.signature: CUresult cuGraphicsSubResourceGetMappedArray(CUarray * pArray, CUgraphicsResource resource, unsigned int arrayIndex, unsigned int mipLevel)
cuGraphicsSubResourceGetMappedArray.doc:
Get an array through which to access a subresource of a mapped graphics resource.

Returns in `*pArray` an array through which the subresource of the mapped graphics resource `resource` which corresponds to array index `arrayIndex` and mipmap level `mipLevel` may be accessed. The value set in `*pArray` may change every time that `resource` is mapped.

If `resource` is not a texture then it cannot be accessed via an array and [CUDA_ERROR_NOT_MAPPED_AS_ARRAY](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggac6c391505e117393cc2558fff6bfc2e9a037f39ebe1bbd16d1b162f4456d507c5) is returned. If `arrayIndex` is not a valid array index for `resource` then [CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_VALUE](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggac6c391505e117393cc2558fff6bfc2e9a90696c86fcee1f536a1ec7d25867feeb) is returned. If `mipLevel` is not a valid mipmap level for `resource` then [CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_VALUE](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggac6c391505e117393cc2558fff6bfc2e9a90696c86fcee1f536a1ec7d25867feeb) is returned. If `resource` is not mapped then [CUDA_ERROR_NOT_MAPPED](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggac6c391505e117393cc2558fff6bfc2e9ae098433b926c9afdb6b6bdf191629447) is returned.

pArray.doc: Returned array through which a subresource of `resource` may be accessed.

arrayIndex.doc: Array index for array textures or cubemap face index as defined by [CUarray_cubemap_face](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ga012fda14b50e7db8798a340627c4c330) for cubemap textures for the subresource to access.

mipLevel.doc: Mipmap level for the subresource to access.

cuGraphicsUnmapResources.signature: CUresult cuGraphicsUnmapResources(unsigned int count, CUgraphicsResource * resources, CUstream hStream)
cuGraphicsUnmapResources.doc:
Unmap graphics resources.

Unmaps the `count` graphics resources in `resources`.

Once unmapped, the resources in `resources` may not be accessed by CUDA until they are mapped again.

This function provides the synchronization guarantee that any CUDA work issued in `stream` before [cuGraphicsUnmapResources()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__GRAPHICS.html#group__cuda__graphics_1ga8e9ff25d071375a0df1cb5aee924af32) will complete before any subsequently issued graphics work begins.

If `resources` includes any duplicate entries then [CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_HANDLE](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggac6c391505e117393cc2558fff6bfc2e9a0fd2e63260c6317ba943af0f7e4b8d21) is returned. If any of `resources` are not presently mapped for access by CUDA then [CUDA_ERROR_NOT_MAPPED](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggac6c391505e117393cc2558fff6bfc2e9ae098433b926c9afdb6b6bdf191629447) is returned.

count.doc: Number of resources to unmap.

cuGraphicsUnregisterResource.doc:
Unregisters a graphics resource for access by CUDA.

Unregisters the graphics resource `resource` so it is not accessible by CUDA unless registered again.

If `resource` is invalid then [CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_HANDLE](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggac6c391505e117393cc2558fff6bfc2e9a0fd2e63260c6317ba943af0f7e4b8d21) is returned.

CU_DEV_SM_RESOURCE_GROUP_LOCALITY_DOMAIN.doc: The SMs must be located on a specific locality domain, specified by localityDomainId.

CU_WORKQUEUE_SCOPE_DEVICE_CTX.doc:
Use all shared workqueue resources across all contexts.

Default driver behavior.

CU_WORKQUEUE_SCOPE_GREEN_CTX_BALANCED.doc: When possible, use non-overlapping workqueue resources with other balanced green contexts.

CU_GREEN_CTX_DEFAULT_STREAM.doc: Creates a default stream to use inside the green context.

cuCtxFromGreenCtx.doc:
Returns a [CUcontext](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1gaf9f5bd81658f866613785b3a0bb7d7d9) handle for a green context.

This API returns in `pContext` a [CUcontext](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1gaf9f5bd81658f866613785b3a0bb7d7d9) handle that represents the specified green context `hCtx`. The returned handle can be passed to CUDA APIs that accept a [CUcontext](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1gaf9f5bd81658f866613785b3a0bb7d7d9) and will be treated as if it were a primary context, while still honoring the resources and configuration associated with `hCtx` as applicable.

Applications that wish to use a green context with CUDA APIs that require a [CUcontext](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1gaf9f5bd81658f866613785b3a0bb7d7d9) must use this API to obtain a handle to a [CUcontext](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1gaf9f5bd81658f866613785b3a0bb7d7d9) representing the green context. Otherwise, passing a green context to such APIs will fail with [CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_CONTEXT](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggac6c391505e117393cc2558fff6bfc2e9aa484e9af32c1e9893ff21f0e0191a12d).

The [CUcontext](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1gaf9f5bd81658f866613785b3a0bb7d7d9) returned by [cuCtxFromGreenCtx](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__GREEN__CONTEXTS.html#group__cuda__green__contexts_1gaf0779ec72ce1d5d7eb003d7d9b25afcb) may be passed to CUDA Driver APIs that accept a [CUcontext](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1gaf9f5bd81658f866613785b3a0bb7d7d9).

This call does not create a new independent context and does not change the underlying context lifetime. The validity of the returned `pContext` is tied to `hCtx`, and no additional destruction or release is required beyond correctly managing `hCtx` with the green context APIs. Destroying `pContext` via cuCtxDestroy is undefined behavior.

cuCtxGetDevResource.signature: CUresult cuCtxGetDevResource(CUcontext hCtx, CUdevResource * resource, CUdevResourceType type)
cuCtxGetDevResource.doc:
Get context resources.

Get the `type` resources available to the context represented by `hCtx`
Note: The API is not supported on 32-bit platforms.

cuDevResourceGenerateDesc.signature: CUresult cuDevResourceGenerateDesc(CUdevResourceDesc * phDesc, CUdevResource * resources, unsigned int nbResources)
cuDevResourceGenerateDesc.doc:
Generate a resource descriptor.

Generates a single resource descriptor with the set of resources specified in `resources`. The generated resource descriptor is necessary for the creation of green contexts via the [cuGreenCtxCreate](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__GREEN__CONTEXTS.html#group__cuda__green__contexts_1gaa6da4f9959fd48d1f1a5cbedbec54e65) API. Resources of the same type can be passed in, provided they meet the requirements as noted below.

A successful API call must have:

The output descriptor `phDesc` will remain valid for the lifetime of the process.

Note: The API is not supported on 32-bit platforms.

resources.doc: Array of resources to be included in the descriptor.

cuDevSmResourceSplit.signature: CUresult cuDevSmResourceSplit(CUdevResource * result, unsigned int nbGroups, const CUdevResource * input, CUdevResource * remainder, unsigned int flags, CU_DEV_SM_RESOURCE_GROUP_PARAMS * groupParams)
cuDevSmResourceSplit.doc:
Splits a [`CUdevResourceType::CU_DEV_RESOURCE_TYPE_SM`] resource into structured groups.

This API will split a resource of [CU_DEV_RESOURCE_TYPE_SM](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__GREEN__CONTEXTS.html#group__cuda__green__contexts_1gga28def480400d3254367d891d58f1375ba3ba3ec7d6c8814ce80b9a633ca2ff332) into `nbGroups` structured device resource groups (the `result` array), as well as an optional `remainder`, according to a set of requirements specified in the `groupParams` array. The term “structured” is a trait that specifies the `result` has SMs that are co-scheduled together. This co-scheduling can be specified via the `coscheduledSmCount` field of the `groupParams` structure, while the `smCount` will specify how many SMs are required in total for that result. The remainder is always “unstructured”, it does not have any set guarantees with respect to co-scheduling and those properties will need to either be queried via the occupancy set of APIs or further split into structured groups by this API.

The API has a discovery mode for use cases where it is difficult to know ahead of time what the SM count should be. Discovery happens when the `smCount` field of a given `groupParams` array entry is set to 0 - the smCount will be filled in by the API with the derived SM count according to the provided `groupParams` fields and constraints. Discovery can be used with both a valid result array and with a NULL `result` pointer value. The latter is useful in situations where the smCount will end up being zero, which is an invalid value to create a result entry with, but allowed for discovery purposes when the `result` is NULL.

The `groupParams` array is evaluated from index 0 to `nbGroups` - 1. For each index in the `groupParams` array, the API will evaluate which SMs may be a good fit based on constraints and assign those SMs to `result`. This evaluation order is important to consider when using discovery mode, as it helps discover the remaining SMs.

For a valid call:

**Example params and their effect:**

A groupParams array element is defined in the following order:

The difference between a catch-all param group as the last entry and the remainder is in two aspects:

Splitting an input into N groups, can be accomplished by repeatedly splitting off 1 group and re-splitting the remainder (a bisect operation). However, it’s recommended to accomplish this with a single call wherever possible.

result.doc: Output array of `CUdevResource` resources. Can be NULL, alongside an smCount of 0, for discovery purpose.

nbGroups.doc: Specifies the number of groups in `result` and `groupParams`.

input.doc: Input SM resource to be split. Must be a valid [`CUdevResourceType::CU_DEV_RESOURCE_TYPE_SM`] resource.

remainder.doc: If splitting the input resource leaves any SMs, the remainder is placed in here.

flags.doc: Flags specifying how the API should behave. The value should be 0 for now.

groupParams.doc: Description of how the SMs should be split and assigned to the corresponding result entry.

cuDevSmResourceSplitByCount.signature: CUresult cuDevSmResourceSplitByCount(CUdevResource * result, unsigned int * nbGroups, const CUdevResource * input, CUdevResource * remainder, unsigned int flags, unsigned int minCount)
cuDevSmResourceSplitByCount.doc:
Splits [`CUdevResourceType::CU_DEV_RESOURCE_TYPE_SM`] resources.

Splits [`CUdevResourceType::CU_DEV_RESOURCE_TYPE_SM`] resources into `nbGroups`, adhering to the minimum SM count specified in `minCount` and the usage flags in `flags`. If `result` is NULL, the API simulates a split and provides the amount of groups that would be created in `nbGroups`. Otherwise, `nbGroups` must point to the amount of elements in `result` and on return, the API will overwrite `nbGroups` with the amount actually created. The groups are written to the array in `result`. `nbGroups` can be less than the total amount if a smaller number of groups is needed.

This API is used to spatially partition the input resource. The input resource needs to come from one of [cuDeviceGetDevResource](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__GREEN__CONTEXTS.html#group__cuda__green__contexts_1ga6115d21604653f4eafb257f725538ab6), [cuCtxGetDevResource](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__GREEN__CONTEXTS.html#group__cuda__green__contexts_1ga00d5b66f04f0591f1c752adb1a924635), or [cuGreenCtxGetDevResource](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__GREEN__CONTEXTS.html#group__cuda__green__contexts_1ga301178535c06137ea8cc9becdbfb90b8). A limitation of the API is that the output results cannot be split again without first creating a descriptor and a green context with that descriptor.

When creating the groups, the API will take into account the performance and functional characteristics of the input resource, and guarantee a split that will create a disjoint set of symmetrical partitions. This may lead to fewer groups created than purely dividing the total SM count by the `minCount` due to cluster requirements or alignment and granularity requirements for the minCount. These requirements can be queried with [cuDeviceGetDevResource](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__GREEN__CONTEXTS.html#group__cuda__green__contexts_1ga6115d21604653f4eafb257f725538ab6), [cuCtxGetDevResource](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__GREEN__CONTEXTS.html#group__cuda__green__contexts_1ga00d5b66f04f0591f1c752adb1a924635), and [cuGreenCtxGetDevResource](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__GREEN__CONTEXTS.html#group__cuda__green__contexts_1ga301178535c06137ea8cc9becdbfb90b8) for [CU_DEV_RESOURCE_TYPE_SM](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__GREEN__CONTEXTS.html#group__cuda__green__contexts_1gga28def480400d3254367d891d58f1375ba3ba3ec7d6c8814ce80b9a633ca2ff332), using the `minSmPartitionSize` and `smCoscheduledAlignment` fields to determine minimum partition size and alignment granularity, respectively.

The `remainder` set does not have the same functional or performance guarantees as the groups in `result`. Its use should be carefully planned and future partitions of the `remainder` set are discouraged.

The following flags are supported:

A successful API call must either have:

Note: The API is not supported on 32-bit platforms.

result.doc: Output array of `CUdevResource` resources. Can be NULL to query the number of groups.

nbGroups.doc: This is a pointer, specifying the number of groups that would be or should be created as described below.

input.doc: Input SM resource to be split. Must be a valid [`CUdevResourceType::CU_DEV_RESOURCE_TYPE_SM`] resource.

remainder.doc: If the input resource cannot be cleanly split among `nbGroups`, the remainder is placed in here. Can be ommitted (NULL) if the user does not need the remaining set.

flags.doc: Flags specifying how these partitions are used or which constraints to abide by when splitting the input. Zero is valid for default behavior.

cuDeviceGetDevResource.signature: CUresult cuDeviceGetDevResource(CUdevice device, CUdevResource * resource, CUdevResourceType type)
cuDeviceGetDevResource.doc:
Get device resources.

Get the `type` resources available to the `device`. This may often be the starting point for further partitioning or configuring of resources.

Note: The API is not supported on 32-bit platforms.

cuGreenCtxCreate.signature: CUresult cuGreenCtxCreate(CUgreenCtx * phCtx, CUdevResourceDesc desc, CUdevice dev, unsigned int flags)
cuGreenCtxCreate.doc:
Creates a green context with a specified set of resources.

This API creates a green context with the resources specified in the descriptor `desc` and returns it in the handle represented by `phCtx`. This API will retain the primary context on device `dev`, which will is released when the green context is destroyed. It is advised to have the primary context active before calling this API to avoid the heavy cost of triggering primary context initialization and deinitialization multiple times.

The API does not set the green context current. In order to set it current, you need to explicitly set it current by first converting the green context to a CUcontext using [cuCtxFromGreenCtx](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__GREEN__CONTEXTS.html#group__cuda__green__contexts_1gaf0779ec72ce1d5d7eb003d7d9b25afcb) and subsequently calling [cuCtxSetCurrent](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__CTX.html#group__cuda__ctx_1gabe562ee6258b4fcc272ca6478ca2a2f7) / cuCtxPushCurrent. It should be noted that a green context can be current to only one thread at a time. There is no internal synchronization to make API calls accessing the same green context from multiple threads work.

Note: The API is not supported on 32-bit platforms.

The supported flags are.

phCtx.doc: Pointer for the output handle to the green context.

desc.doc: Descriptor generated via [cuDevResourceGenerateDesc](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__GREEN__CONTEXTS.html#group__cuda__green__contexts_1ga1ea7743fd633d2e2dd92eb1c84c4fbc5) which contains the set of resources to be used.

dev.doc: Device on which to create the green context.

flags.doc: One of the supported green context creation flags.

cuGreenCtxDestroy.doc:
Destroys a green context.

Destroys the green context, releasing the primary context of the device that this green context was created for. Any resources provisioned for this green context (that were initially available via the resource descriptor) are released as well. The API does not destroy streams created via [cuGreenCtxStreamCreate](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__GREEN__CONTEXTS.html#group__cuda__green__contexts_1ga569b9e947b0f143f6ed9397a12046a8a), [cuStreamCreate](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__STREAM.html#group__cuda__stream_1gaa581f0c5833e21ded8b5a56594e243f4), or [cuStreamCreateWithPriority](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__STREAM.html#group__cuda__stream_1ga95c1a8c7c3dacb13091692dd9c7f7471). Users are expected to destroy these streams explicitly using cuStreamDestroy to avoid resource leaks. Once the green context is destroyed, any subsequent API calls involving these streams will return [CUDA_ERROR_STREAM_DETACHED](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggac6c391505e117393cc2558fff6bfc2e9aaad337be88462a55bdcfcbff87d788c6) with the exception of the following APIs:

Additionally, the API will invalidate all active captures on these streams.

cuGreenCtxGetDevResource.signature: CUresult cuGreenCtxGetDevResource(CUgreenCtx hCtx, CUdevResource * resource, CUdevResourceType type)
cuGreenCtxGetDevResource.doc:
Get green context resources.

Get the `type` resources available to the green context represented by `hCtx`.

hCtx.doc: Green context to get resource for.

cuGreenCtxGetId.signature: CUresult cuGreenCtxGetId(CUgreenCtx greenCtx, unsigned long long * greenCtxId)
cuGreenCtxGetId.doc:
Returns the unique Id associated with the green context supplied.

Returns in `greenCtxId` the unique Id which is associated with a given green context. The Id is unique for the life of the program for this instance of CUDA. If green context is supplied as NULL and the current context is set to a green context, the Id of the current green context is returned.

greenCtx.doc: Green context for which to obtain the Id.

greenCtxId.doc: Pointer to store the Id of the green context.

cuGreenCtxRecordEvent.doc:
Records an event.

Captures in `hEvent` all the activities of the green context of `hCtx` at the time of this call. `hEvent` and `hCtx` must be from the same primary context otherwise [CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_HANDLE](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggac6c391505e117393cc2558fff6bfc2e9a0fd2e63260c6317ba943af0f7e4b8d21) is returned. Calls such as [cuEventQuery()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__EVENT.html#group__cuda__event_1ga6f0704d755066b0ee705749ae911deef) or [cuGreenCtxWaitEvent()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__GREEN__CONTEXTS.html#group__cuda__green__contexts_1ga6b26172117084fd024f1396fb66a8ffd) will then examine or wait for completion of the work that was captured. Uses of `hCtx` after this call do not modify `hEvent`.

hCtx.doc: Green context to record event for.

cuGreenCtxStreamCreate.signature: CUresult cuGreenCtxStreamCreate(CUstream * phStream, CUgreenCtx greenCtx, unsigned int flags, int priority)
cuGreenCtxStreamCreate.doc:
Create a stream for use in the green context.

Creates a stream for use in the specified green context `greenCtx` and returns a handle in `phStream`. The stream can be destroyed by calling cuStreamDestroy(). Note that the API ignores the context that is current to the calling thread and creates a stream in the specified green context `greenCtx`.

The supported values for `flags` are:

Specifying `priority` affects the scheduling priority of work in the stream. Priorities provide a hint to preferentially run work with higher priority when possible, but do not preempt already-running work or provide any other functional guarantee on execution order. `priority` follows a convention where lower numbers represent higher priorities. ‘0’ represents default priority. The range of meaningful numerical priorities can be queried using [cuCtxGetStreamPriorityRange](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__CTX.html#group__cuda__ctx_1ga137920ab61a71be6ce67605b9f294091). If the specified priority is outside the numerical range returned by [cuCtxGetStreamPriorityRange](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__CTX.html#group__cuda__ctx_1ga137920ab61a71be6ce67605b9f294091), it will automatically be clamped to the lowest or the highest number in the range.

greenCtx.doc: Green context for which to create the stream for.

flags.doc: Flags for stream creation. [`CUstream_flags::CU_STREAM_NON_BLOCKING`] must be specified.

priority.doc: Stream priority. Lower numbers represent higher priorities. See [cuCtxGetStreamPriorityRange](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__CTX.html#group__cuda__ctx_1ga137920ab61a71be6ce67605b9f294091) for more information about meaningful stream priorities that can be passed.

cuGreenCtxWaitEvent.doc:
Make a green context wait on an event.

Makes all future work submitted to green context `hCtx` wait for all work captured in `hEvent`. The synchronization will be performed on the device and will not block the calling CPU thread. See [cuGreenCtxRecordEvent()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__GREEN__CONTEXTS.html#group__cuda__green__contexts_1ga9dd087071cc217ad7ebda6df96d2ee40) or [cuEventRecord()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__EVENT.html#group__cuda__event_1ga95424d3be52c4eb95d83861b70fb89d1), for details on what is captured by an event.

cuStreamGetDevResource.signature: CUresult cuStreamGetDevResource(CUstream hStream, CUdevResource * resource, CUdevResourceType type)
cuStreamGetDevResource.doc:
Get stream resources.

Get the `type` resources available to the `hStream` and store them in `resource`.

Note: The API will return [CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_RESOURCE_TYPE](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggac6c391505e117393cc2558fff6bfc2e9a4ec23220911f54aa1e66d8bcf86ec7ba) is `type` is [`CUdevResourceType::CU_DEV_RESOURCE_TYPE_WORKQUEUE_CONFIG`] or [`CUdevResourceType::CU_DEV_RESOURCE_TYPE_WORKQUEUE`].

cuStreamGetGreenCtx.doc:
Query the green context associated with a stream.

Returns the CUDA green context that the stream is associated with, or NULL if the stream is not associated with any green context.

The stream handle `hStream` can refer to any of the following.

hStream.doc: Handle to the stream to be queried.

phCtx.doc: Returned green context associated with the stream.

CUdevResourceDesc.doc: An opaque descriptor handle. The descriptor encapsulates multiple created and configured resources. Created via [cuDevResourceGenerateDesc](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__GREEN__CONTEXTS.html#group__cuda__green__contexts_1ga1ea7743fd633d2e2dd92eb1c84c4fbc5).

cuInit.doc:
Initialize the CUDA driver API Initializes the driver API and must be called before any other function from the driver API in the current process.

Currently, the `Flags` parameter must be 0. If [cuInit()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__INITIALIZE.html#group__cuda__initialize_1ga0a2f1517e1bd8502c7194c3a8c134bc3) has not been called, any function from the driver API will return [CUDA_ERROR_NOT_INITIALIZED](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggac6c391505e117393cc2558fff6bfc2e9a8feb999f0af99b4a25ab26b3866f4df8).

Note: cuInit preloads various libraries needed for JIT compilation. To opt-out of this behavior, set the environment variable CUDA_FORCE_PRELOAD_LIBRARIES=0. CUDA will lazily load JIT libraries as needed. To disable JIT entirely, set the environment variable CUDA_DISABLE_JIT=1.

cuKernelGetAttribute.signature: CUresult cuKernelGetAttribute(int * pi, CUfunction_attribute attrib, CUkernel kernel, CUdevice dev)
cuKernelGetAttribute.doc:
Returns information about a kernel.

Returns in `*pi` the integer value of the attribute `attrib` for the kernel `kernel` for the requested device `dev`. The supported attributes are.

dev.doc: Device to query attribute of.

cuKernelGetFunction.doc:
Returns a function handle.

Returns in `pFunc` the handle of the function for the requested kernel `kernel` and the current context. If function handle is not found, the call returns [CUDA_ERROR_NOT_FOUND](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggac6c391505e117393cc2558fff6bfc2e9aaf1cadbeb21d3a78115ca211ba44c053).

kernel.doc: Kernel to retrieve function for the requested context.

cuKernelGetLibrary.doc:
Returns a library handle.

Returns in `pLib` the handle of the library for the requested kernel `kernel`.

cuKernelGetName.signature: CUresult cuKernelGetName(const char * * name, CUkernel hfunc)
cuKernelGetName.doc:
Returns the function name for a [CUkernel](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ga612028921e5736db673e4307589989ed) handle.

Returns in `**name` the function name associated with the kernel handle `hfunc`. The function name is returned as a null-terminated string. The returned name is only valid when the kernel handle is valid. If the library is unloaded or reloaded, one must call the API again to get the updated name. This API may return a mangled name if the function is not declared as having C linkage. If either `**name` or `hfunc` is NULL, [CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_VALUE](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggac6c391505e117393cc2558fff6bfc2e9a90696c86fcee1f536a1ec7d25867feeb) is returned.

name.doc: The returned name of the function.

hfunc.doc: The function handle to retrieve the name for.

cuKernelGetParamCount.doc:
Returns the number of parameters used by the kernel.

Queries the number of kernel parameters used by `kernel` and returns it in `paramCount`.

paramCount.doc: Returns the number of parameters used by the function.

cuKernelGetParamInfo.signature: CUresult cuKernelGetParamInfo(CUkernel kernel, size_t paramIndex, size_t * paramOffset, size_t * paramSize)
cuKernelGetParamInfo.doc:
Returns the offset and size of a kernel parameter in the device-side parameter layout.

Queries the kernel parameter at `paramIndex` into `kernel's` list of parameters, and returns in `paramOffset` and `paramSize` the offset and size, respectively, where the parameter will reside in the device-side parameter layout. This information can be used to update kernel node parameters from the device via ::cudaGraphKernelNodeSetParam() and ::cudaGraphKernelNodeUpdatesApply(). `paramIndex` must be less than the number of parameters that `kernel` takes. `paramSize` can be set to NULL if only the parameter offset is desired.

paramOffset.doc: Returns the offset into the device-side parameter layout at which the parameter resides.

paramSize.doc: Optionally returns the size of the parameter in the device-side parameter layout.

cuKernelSetAttribute.signature: CUresult cuKernelSetAttribute(CUfunction_attribute attrib, int val, CUkernel kernel, CUdevice dev)
cuKernelSetAttribute.doc:
Sets information about a kernel.

This call sets the value of a specified attribute `attrib` on the kernel `kernel` for the requested device `dev` to an integer value specified by `val`. This function returns [`CUresult::CUDA_SUCCESS`] if the new value of the attribute could be successfully set. If the set fails, this call will return an error. Not all attributes can have values set. Attempting to set a value on a read-only attribute will result in an error ([`CUresult::CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_VALUE`])

Note that attributes set using [cuFuncSetAttribute()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__EXEC.html#group__cuda__exec_1ga0e37dce0173bc883aa1e5b14dd747f26) will override the attribute set by this API irrespective of whether the call to [cuFuncSetAttribute()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__EXEC.html#group__cuda__exec_1ga0e37dce0173bc883aa1e5b14dd747f26) is made before or after this API call. However, [cuKernelGetAttribute()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__LIBRARY.html#group__cuda__library_1gad98317cb151b99fbd95767418122071f) will always return the attribute value set by this API.

Supported attributes are.

dev.doc: Device to set attribute of.

cuKernelSetCacheConfig.signature: CUresult cuKernelSetCacheConfig(CUkernel kernel, CUfunc_cache config, CUdevice dev)
cuKernelSetCacheConfig.doc:
Sets the preferred cache configuration for a device kernel.

On devices where the L1 cache and shared memory use the same hardware resources, this sets through `config` the preferred cache configuration for the device kernel `kernel` on the requested device `dev`. This is only a preference. The driver will use the requested configuration if possible, but it is free to choose a different configuration if required to execute `kernel`. Any context-wide preference set via [cuCtxSetCacheConfig()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__CTX.html#group__cuda__ctx_1ga54699acf7e2ef27279d013ca2095f4a3) will be overridden by this per-kernel setting.

Note that attributes set using [cuFuncSetCacheConfig()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__EXEC.html#group__cuda__exec_1ga40f8c11e81def95dc0072a375f965681) will override the attribute set by this API irrespective of whether the call to [cuFuncSetCacheConfig()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__EXEC.html#group__cuda__exec_1ga40f8c11e81def95dc0072a375f965681) is made before or after this API call.

This setting does nothing on devices where the size of the L1 cache and shared memory are fixed.

Launching a kernel with a different preference than the most recent preference setting may insert a device-side synchronization point.

The supported cache configurations are.

dev.doc: Device to set attribute of.

cuLibraryEnumerateKernels.signature: CUresult cuLibraryEnumerateKernels(CUkernel * kernels, unsigned int numKernels, CUlibrary lib)
cuLibraryEnumerateKernels.doc:
Retrieve the kernel handles within a library.

Returns in `kernels` a maximum number of `numKernels` kernel handles within `lib`. The returned kernel handle becomes invalid when the library is unloaded.

kernels.doc: Buffer where the kernel handles are returned to.

numKernels.doc: Maximum number of kernel handles may be returned to the buffer.

cuLibraryGetGlobal.signature: CUresult cuLibraryGetGlobal(CUdeviceptr * dptr, size_t * bytes, CUlibrary library, const char * name)
cuLibraryGetGlobal.doc:
Returns a global device pointer.

Returns in `*dptr` and `*bytes` the base pointer and size of the global with name `name` for the requested library `library` and the current context. If no global for the requested name `name` exists, the call returns [CUDA_ERROR_NOT_FOUND](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggac6c391505e117393cc2558fff6bfc2e9aaf1cadbeb21d3a78115ca211ba44c053). One of the parameters `dptr` or `bytes` (not both) can be NULL in which case it is ignored.

dptr.doc: Returned global device pointer for the requested context.

cuLibraryGetKernel.signature: CUresult cuLibraryGetKernel(CUkernel * pKernel, CUlibrary library, const char * name)
cuLibraryGetKernel.doc:
Returns a kernel handle.

Returns in `pKernel` the handle of the kernel with name `name` located in library `library`. If kernel handle is not found, the call returns [CUDA_ERROR_NOT_FOUND](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggac6c391505e117393cc2558fff6bfc2e9aaf1cadbeb21d3a78115ca211ba44c053).

cuLibraryGetKernelCount.signature: CUresult cuLibraryGetKernelCount(unsigned int * count, CUlibrary lib)
cuLibraryGetKernelCount.doc:
Returns the number of kernels within a library.

Returns in `count` the number of kernels in `lib`.

count.doc: Number of kernels found within the library.

cuLibraryGetManaged.signature: CUresult cuLibraryGetManaged(CUdeviceptr * dptr, size_t * bytes, CUlibrary library, const char * name)
cuLibraryGetManaged.doc:
Returns a pointer to managed memory.

Returns in `*dptr` and `*bytes` the base pointer and size of the managed memory with name `name` for the requested library `library`. If no managed memory with the requested name `name` exists, the call returns [CUDA_ERROR_NOT_FOUND](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggac6c391505e117393cc2558fff6bfc2e9aaf1cadbeb21d3a78115ca211ba44c053). One of the parameters `dptr` or `bytes` (not both) can be NULL in which case it is ignored. Note that managed memory for library `library` is shared across devices and is registered when the library is loaded into at least one context.

dptr.doc: Returned pointer to the managed memory.

library.doc: Library to retrieve managed memory from.

name.doc: Name of managed memory to retrieve.

cuLibraryGetModule.doc:
Returns a module handle.

Returns in `pMod` the module handle associated with the current context located in library `library`. If module handle is not found, the call returns [CUDA_ERROR_NOT_FOUND](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggac6c391505e117393cc2558fff6bfc2e9aaf1cadbeb21d3a78115ca211ba44c053).

cuLibraryGetUnifiedFunction.signature: CUresult cuLibraryGetUnifiedFunction(void * * fptr, CUlibrary library, const char * symbol)
cuLibraryGetUnifiedFunction.doc:
Returns a pointer to a unified function.

Returns in `*fptr` the function pointer to a unified function denoted by `symbol`. If no unified function with name `symbol` exists, the call returns [CUDA_ERROR_NOT_FOUND](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggac6c391505e117393cc2558fff6bfc2e9aaf1cadbeb21d3a78115ca211ba44c053). If there is no device with attribute [CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_UNIFIED_FUNCTION_POINTERS](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggae12b8a782bebe21b1ac0091bf9f4e2a3af64e13496d96670082083817ba6c6266) present in the system, the call may return [CUDA_ERROR_NOT_FOUND](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggac6c391505e117393cc2558fff6bfc2e9aaf1cadbeb21d3a78115ca211ba44c053).

fptr.doc: Returned pointer to a unified function.

library.doc: Library to retrieve function pointer memory from.

symbol.doc: Name of function pointer to retrieve.

cuLibraryLoadData.signature: CUresult cuLibraryLoadData(CUlibrary * library, const void * code, CUjit_option * jitOptions, void * * jitOptionsValues, unsigned int numJitOptions, CUlibraryOption * libraryOptions, void * * libraryOptionValues, unsigned int numLibraryOptions)
cuLibraryLoadData.doc:
Load a library with specified code and options.

Takes a pointer `code` and loads the corresponding library `library` based on the application defined library loading mode:

These environment variables are described in the CUDA programming guide under the “CUDA environment variables” section.

The `code` may be a *cubin* or *fatbin* as output by **nvcc**, or a NULL-terminated *PTX*, either as output by **nvcc** or hand-written, or *Tile* IR data. A fatbin should also contain relocatable code when doing separate compilation.

Options are passed as an array via `jitOptions` and any corresponding parameters are passed in `jitOptionsValues`. The number of total JIT options is supplied via `numJitOptions`. Any outputs will be returned via `jitOptionsValues`.

Library load options are passed as an array via `libraryOptions` and any corresponding parameters are passed in `libraryOptionValues`. The number of total library load options is supplied via `numLibraryOptions`.

cuLibraryLoadFromFile.signature: CUresult cuLibraryLoadFromFile(CUlibrary * library, const char * fileName, CUjit_option * jitOptions, void * * jitOptionsValues, unsigned int numJitOptions, CUlibraryOption * libraryOptions, void * * libraryOptionValues, unsigned int numLibraryOptions)
cuLibraryLoadFromFile.doc:
Load a library with specified file and options.

Takes a pointer `code` and loads the corresponding library `library` based on the application defined library loading mode:

These environment variables are described in the CUDA programming guide under the “CUDA environment variables” section.

The file should be a *cubin* file as output by **nvcc**, or a *PTX* file either as output by **nvcc** or handwritten, or a *fatbin* file as output by **nvcc** or hand-written, or *Tile* IR file. A fatbin should also contain relocatable code when doing separate compilation.

Options are passed as an array via `jitOptions` and any corresponding parameters are passed in `jitOptionsValues`. The number of total options is supplied via `numJitOptions`. Any outputs will be returned via `jitOptionsValues`.

Library load options are passed as an array via `libraryOptions` and any corresponding parameters are passed in `libraryOptionValues`. The number of total library load options is supplied via `numLibraryOptions`.

cuLibraryUnload.doc:
Unloads a library.

Unloads the library specified with `library`.

CU_LOGICAL_ENDPOINT_FLAG_NONE.doc: Default flag for logical endpoint construction.

CU_LOGICAL_ENDPOINT_FLAG_COUNTED_OPS.doc: Indicate the programmer’s intention to use counted operations with the logical endpoint.

CUlogicalEndpointIpcHandleType.doc: IPC handle types that can be requested/queried for a given logical endpoint.

cuLogicalEndpointAddDevice.doc:
Associates a device to a multicast logical endpoint.

Associates a device to a logical endpoint. The type of the logical endpoint must be [`CUlogicalEndpointType::CU_LOGICAL_ENDPOINT_TYPE_MULTICAST`]. The added device will be a part of the multicast team of size specified by CUlogicalEndpointProp::multicast::numDevices during [cuLogicalEndpointCreate](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__LOGICAL__ENDPOINT.html#group__cuda__logical__endpoint_1gaa71ca82c275168ff93eff1df623042f7). The association of the device to the multicast logical endpoint is permanent during the life time of the multicast logical endpoint. All devices must be added to the multicast logical endpoint before any memory can be bound to any device in the team. A multicast logical endpoint will not be ready for use until all devices have been added. User can query whether the logical endpoint is ready for use via [cuLogicalEndpointQuery](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__LOGICAL__ENDPOINT.html#group__cuda__logical__endpoint_1gadff0539c09f0eda8e9cce465c80bcbcb).

This call may fail with [CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_DEVICE](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggac6c391505e117393cc2558fff6bfc2e9a6f047e7215788ca96c81af92a04bfb6c) if the device specified by `dev` does not belong to the same clique as the other devices previously added to this multicast logical endpoint.

leId.doc: Logical endpoint id representing a multicast logical endpoint.

dev.doc: Device that will be associated with the multicast logical endpoint.

cuLogicalEndpointBindAddr.signature: CUresult cuLogicalEndpointBindAddr(CUlogicalEndpointId leId, CUdevice dev, cuuint64_t offset, void * ptr, cuuint64_t size, unsigned long long flags)
cuLogicalEndpointBindAddr.doc:
Bind a memory allocation represented by a virtual address to a logical endpoint.

Binds the memory allocation specified by its mapped address `ptr` to a logical endpoint represented by `leId` at the offset `offset`. The memory must have been allocated via [cuMemCreate](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__VA.html#group__cuda__va_1ga899d69a862bba36449789c64b430dc7c) or ::cudaMallocAsync. The intended `size` of the bind, the `offset` in the logical endpoint range and `ptr` must be multiples of the value for `bindAlignment` as returned by [cuLogicalEndpointGetLimits](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__LOGICAL__ENDPOINT.html#group__cuda__logical__endpoint_1gafb9173d8bc61d60c6e49729947d3594a).

The `size` cannot be larger than the size of the allocated memory. Similarly the `size` + `offset` cannot be larger than the total size of the logical endpoint.

For device memory, i.e., type [CU_MEM_LOCATION_TYPE_DEVICE](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1gga75cfd5b9fa5c1c6ee2be2547bfbe882eaa4409aa6b414995d628a320eafbbbb6e), the memory allocation must have been created on the device specified by `dev`. For host NUMA memory, i.e., type [CU_MEM_LOCATION_TYPE_HOST_NUMA](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1gga75cfd5b9fa5c1c6ee2be2547bfbe882eab61a1d3409ed83a43b5706cc004ac861), the memory allocation must have been created on the CPU NUMA node closest to `dev`. That is, the value returned when querying [CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_HOST_NUMA_ID](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggae12b8a782bebe21b1ac0091bf9f4e2a3a2583f8184b09441b3c83b1bee7849556) for `dev`, must be the CPU NUMA node where the memory was allocated.

For multicast endpoints, the device named by `dev` must have been added to the multicast team via [cuLogicalEndpointAddDevice](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__LOGICAL__ENDPOINT.html#group__cuda__logical__endpoint_1gad2d33cb39d6fafbde7a1c7fd73688b66).

For unicast endpoints the device named by `dev` must be the owner device specified during [cuLogicalEndpointCreate](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__LOGICAL__ENDPOINT.html#group__cuda__logical__endpoint_1gaa71ca82c275168ff93eff1df623042f7) via ::CUlogicalEndpointProp::unicast::device.

Externally shareable as well as imported multicast endpoints can be bound only to externally shareable memory. Imported unicast endpoints cannot be bound to any memory.

This call will return [CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_VALUE](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggac6c391505e117393cc2558fff6bfc2e9a90696c86fcee1f536a1ec7d25867feeb) if [cuLogicalEndpointQuery](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__LOGICAL__ENDPOINT.html#group__cuda__logical__endpoint_1gadff0539c09f0eda8e9cce465c80bcbcb) has not been called for the logical endpoint to ensure that the endpoint is ready for memory binding.

Note that this call will return [CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggac6c391505e117393cc2558fff6bfc2e9a264c50688ed110e8476b591befe60c02) if there are insufficient resources required to perform the bind. This call may also return [CUDA_ERROR_SYSTEM_NOT_READY](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggac6c391505e117393cc2558fff6bfc2e9a659c7730ee79fae8262043448f2ce1e3) if the necessary system software is not initialized or running. This call may return [CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_STATE](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggac6c391505e117393cc2558fff6bfc2e9af5fd9c15b97a258f341bab23b0b505a5) if the system configuration is in an illegal state. In such cases, to continue using logical endpoints, verify that the system configuration is in a valid state and all required driver daemons are running properly.

leId.doc: Logical endpoint to which memory will be associated.

dev.doc: Device on which the memory will be bound to the logical endpoint.

offset.doc: Offset into the logical endpoint space.

ptr.doc: Virtual address of the memory allocation.

size.doc: Size of memory that will be bound to the logical endpoint.

flags.doc: Flags for future use, must be zero for now.

cuLogicalEndpointBindMem.signature: CUresult cuLogicalEndpointBindMem(CUlogicalEndpointId leId, CUdevice dev, cuuint64_t offset, CUmemGenericAllocationHandle memHandle, cuuint64_t memOffset, cuuint64_t size, unsigned long long flags)
cuLogicalEndpointBindMem.doc:
Binds memory object represented by a handle to the logical endpoint.

Binds the memory allocation specified by `memHandle` to a logical endpoint represented by `leId` at the offset `offset`. The memory must have been allocated via [cuMemCreate](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__VA.html#group__cuda__va_1ga899d69a862bba36449789c64b430dc7c). The intended `size` of the bind, the offset in the logical endpoint range `offset` and the offset in the memory handle `memOffset` must be multiples of the value for `bindAlignment` as returned by [cuLogicalEndpointGetLimits](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__LOGICAL__ENDPOINT.html#group__cuda__logical__endpoint_1gafb9173d8bc61d60c6e49729947d3594a).

The `size` + `memOffset` cannot be larger than the size of the allocated memory. Similarly the `size` + `offset` cannot be larger than the total size of the logical endpoint.

For device memory, i.e., type [CU_MEM_LOCATION_TYPE_DEVICE](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1gga75cfd5b9fa5c1c6ee2be2547bfbe882eaa4409aa6b414995d628a320eafbbbb6e), the memory allocation must have been created on the device specified by `dev`. For host NUMA memory, i.e., type [CU_MEM_LOCATION_TYPE_HOST_NUMA](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1gga75cfd5b9fa5c1c6ee2be2547bfbe882eab61a1d3409ed83a43b5706cc004ac861), the memory allocation must have been created on the CPU NUMA node closest to `dev`. That is, the value returned when querying [CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_HOST_NUMA_ID](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggae12b8a782bebe21b1ac0091bf9f4e2a3a2583f8184b09441b3c83b1bee7849556) for `dev`, must be the CPU NUMA node where the memory was allocated.

For multicast endpoints, the device named by `dev` must have been added to the multicast team via [cuLogicalEndpointAddDevice](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__LOGICAL__ENDPOINT.html#group__cuda__logical__endpoint_1gad2d33cb39d6fafbde7a1c7fd73688b66).

For unicast endpoints the device named by `dev` must be the owner device specified during [cuLogicalEndpointCreate](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__LOGICAL__ENDPOINT.html#group__cuda__logical__endpoint_1gaa71ca82c275168ff93eff1df623042f7) via ::CUlogicalEndpointProp::unicast::device.

Externally shareable as well as imported multicast endpoints can be bound only to externally shareable memory. Imported unicast endpoints cannot be bound to any memory.

This call will return [CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_VALUE](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggac6c391505e117393cc2558fff6bfc2e9a90696c86fcee1f536a1ec7d25867feeb) if [cuLogicalEndpointQuery](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__LOGICAL__ENDPOINT.html#group__cuda__logical__endpoint_1gadff0539c09f0eda8e9cce465c80bcbcb) has not been called for the logical endpoint to ensure that the endpoint is ready for memory binding.

Note that this call will return [CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggac6c391505e117393cc2558fff6bfc2e9a264c50688ed110e8476b591befe60c02) if there are insufficient resources required to perform the bind. This call may also return [CUDA_ERROR_SYSTEM_NOT_READY](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggac6c391505e117393cc2558fff6bfc2e9a659c7730ee79fae8262043448f2ce1e3) if the necessary system software is not initialized or running. This call may return [CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_STATE](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggac6c391505e117393cc2558fff6bfc2e9af5fd9c15b97a258f341bab23b0b505a5) if the system configuration is in an illegal state. In such cases, to continue using logical endpoints, verify that the system configuration is in a valid state and all required driver daemons are running properly.

leId.doc: Logical endpoint to which memory will be associated.

dev.doc: Device on which the memory will be bound to the logical endpoint.

offset.doc: Offset into the logical endpoint space.

memOffset.doc: Offset into the memory for the attachment.

size.doc: Size of memory that will be bound to the logical endpoint.

flags.doc: Flags for future use, must be zero for now.

cuLogicalEndpointCreate.doc:
Creates a logical endpoint with the requested properties and associates it with the logical endpoint id.

This creates a logical endpoint as described by `prop`. The number of participating devices is determined by the [CUlogicalEndpointProp::type](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/structCUlogicalEndpointProp.html#structculogicalendpointprop_1ad1eeea7a8e5f814385197b3c4125680e). If the type is [`CUlogicalEndpointType::CU_LOGICAL_ENDPOINT_TYPE_UNICAST`] then ::CUlogicalEndpointProp::unicast::device specifies the owner device of the unicast logical endpoint. If the type is [`CUlogicalEndpointType::CU_LOGICAL_ENDPOINT_TYPE_MULTICAST`] then ::CUlogicalEndpointProp::multicast::numDevices specifies the number of devices in the multicast logical endpoint team.

Devices can be added to a multicast logical endpoint via [cuLogicalEndpointAddDevice](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__LOGICAL__ENDPOINT.html#group__cuda__logical__endpoint_1gad2d33cb39d6fafbde7a1c7fd73688b66). After all the participating devices have been added, a call to [cuLogicalEndpointQuery](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__LOGICAL__ENDPOINT.html#group__cuda__logical__endpoint_1gadff0539c09f0eda8e9cce465c80bcbcb) must be made to ensure that the logical endpoint is ready for memory binding and access.

A unicast logical endpoint does not have a notion of adding devices via [cuLogicalEndpointAddDevice](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__LOGICAL__ENDPOINT.html#group__cuda__logical__endpoint_1gad2d33cb39d6fafbde7a1c7fd73688b66). However, a call to [cuLogicalEndpointQuery](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__LOGICAL__ENDPOINT.html#group__cuda__logical__endpoint_1gadff0539c09f0eda8e9cce465c80bcbcb) must still be made to ensure that the logical endpoint is ready for memory binding and access.

Memory is bound to the logical endpoint via either [cuLogicalEndpointBindAddr](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__LOGICAL__ENDPOINT.html#group__cuda__logical__endpoint_1gadc6b78cf705fb44fe83c310b5aaa2d51) or [cuLogicalEndpointBindMem](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__LOGICAL__ENDPOINT.html#group__cuda__logical__endpoint_1ga9a85919bc6c52d1c63a0bb4acd32cb6e), and can be unbound via [cuLogicalEndpointUnbind](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__LOGICAL__ENDPOINT.html#group__cuda__logical__endpoint_1gab1c8b71fe516b61a959ad1c0a6fadddc). The total amount of memory that can be bound per device is specified by [CUlogicalEndpointProp::size](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/structCUlogicalEndpointProp.html#structculogicalendpointprop_1a3b553dde52f259ef1f08cdad07e4f82d). This size must be a multiple of the value for `bindAlignment` as returned by [cuLogicalEndpointGetLimits](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__LOGICAL__ENDPOINT.html#group__cuda__logical__endpoint_1gafb9173d8bc61d60c6e49729947d3594a). The maximum size for the logical endpoint cannot exceed the value for `maxSize` as returned by [cuLogicalEndpointGetLimits](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__LOGICAL__ENDPOINT.html#group__cuda__logical__endpoint_1gafb9173d8bc61d60c6e49729947d3594a). The bind alignment and maximum size depend on the properties of the logical endpoint.

leId.doc: Logical endpoint id that will be associated with the newly created logical endpoint.

prop.doc: Properties of the logical endpoint to create.

cuLogicalEndpointDestroy.doc:
Removes the association of the logical endpoint from the logical endpoint id.

Removes the association between the logical endpoint id and the logical endpoint resources. Any memory bound by this process to any device associated with the logical endpoint will be unbound. If this was the last reference to the logical endpoint, all associated resources will be destroyed.

cuLogicalEndpointExport.signature: CUresult cuLogicalEndpointExport(void * handle, CUlogicalEndpointId leId, CUlogicalEndpointIpcHandleType handleType)
cuLogicalEndpointExport.doc:
Exports a logical endpoint associated with leId to an IPC handle.

Given a logical endpoint id `leId`, create a shareable handle `handle` that can be used to share the logical endpoint with other processes. The recipient process can convert the shareable handle back into a logical endpoint id using [cuLogicalEndpointImport](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__LOGICAL__ENDPOINT.html#group__cuda__logical__endpoint_1ga40fafd9e45546a266eeaa41f83de5d2b). The implementation of what this `handle` is and how it can be transfered is defined by the requested handle type in `handletype`.

handle.doc: Pointer to the location in which to store the requested handle type.

leId.doc: Logical endpoint id of logical endpoint.

handleType.doc: Type of shareable handle requested. Defines type and size of the handle output parameter.

cuLogicalEndpointGetLimits.signature: CUresult cuLogicalEndpointGetLimits(cuuint64_t * bindAlignment, cuuint64_t * maxSize, const CUlogicalEndpointProp * prop)
cuLogicalEndpointGetLimits.doc:
Calculates the minimum alignment and the maximum size for the given logical endpoint properties.

The `bindAlignment` can be used as a multiple for size and bind offset values. The `maxSize` is the maximum size of the logical endpoint. If `maxSize` is less than [CUlogicalEndpointProp](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/structCUlogicalEndpointProp.html#structculogicalendpointprop):size the user must adjust the request to the smaller value.

bindAlignment.doc: Minimum alignment granularity of the proposed logical endpoint.

maxSize.doc: Maximum size of the logical endpoint.

cuLogicalEndpointIdRelease.doc:
Releases a range of logical endpoint ids.

Releases up to `count` logical endpoint ids starting at `baseLeId`. The range of ids represented by [`baseLeId`, `baseLeId` + `count`) must all be previously reserved. All logical endpoints in the range must be destroyed before they can be released.

baseLeId.doc: First logical endpoint id to be released back to the system.

count.doc: Number of logical endpoint ids to release back to the system.

cuLogicalEndpointIdReserve.doc:
Reserves a range of logical endpoint ids.

Reserves a range of logical endpoint ids starting at `*baseLeId` and extending for `count`. The reserved ids can be used to create or import logical endpoints via [cuLogicalEndpointCreate](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__LOGICAL__ENDPOINT.html#group__cuda__logical__endpoint_1gaa71ca82c275168ff93eff1df623042f7) or [cuLogicalEndpointImport](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__LOGICAL__ENDPOINT.html#group__cuda__logical__endpoint_1ga40fafd9e45546a266eeaa41f83de5d2b) respectively.

baseLeId.doc: If [cuLogicalEndpointIdReserve](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__LOGICAL__ENDPOINT.html#group__cuda__logical__endpoint_1gabef8117440c51e482fb455d6a649bd97) returns [`CUresult::CUDA_SUCCESS`], \*baseLeId contains the base logical endpoint id of the reserved logical endpoint id range.

count.doc: The number of logical endpoint ids to reserve.

cuLogicalEndpointImport.signature: CUresult cuLogicalEndpointImport(CUlogicalEndpointId leId, const void * handle, CUlogicalEndpointIpcHandleType handleType)
cuLogicalEndpointImport.doc:
Imports a logical endpoint from the given IPC handle and associates it with a logical endpoint id.

Imports a logical endpoint from the given IPC `handle` and associates it with the logical endpoint id specified by `leId`.

If the current process cannot support the logical endpoint described by the shareable handle, this API will error as [CUDA_ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggac6c391505e117393cc2558fff6bfc2e9a54756ae7ade0dfd09faeccb513dd831b). If `handle` is of type [`CUlogicalEndpointIpcHandleType::CU_LOGICAL_ENDPOINT_IPC_HANDLE_TYPE_FABRIC`] and the importer process does not have access permissions, then [CUDA_ERROR_NOT_PERMITTED](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggac6c391505e117393cc2558fff6bfc2e9ae23d0197c490ec332a43e55b167968a3) will be returned.

leId.doc: Logical endpoint id that will be used to access the exported logical endpoint.

handle.doc: Shareable handle representing the logical endpoint that is to be imported.

handleType.doc: Handle type of the exported handle.

cuLogicalEndpointQuery.signature: CUresult cuLogicalEndpointQuery(CUlogicalEndpointId leId, cuuint32_t count, int * queryStatus)
cuLogicalEndpointQuery.doc:
Determines if all logical endpoints in the range have been successfully constructed.

Queries the driver to determine if all logical endpoints in the given range starting at `leId` and extending for `count` have been successfully constructed.

Provides a mechanism to ensure that it is safe to begin using a logical endpoint ID. Using a logical endpoint ID before verifying that it is fully constructed can result in undefined behavior.

This is not a blocking API, it returns immediately with a `queryStatus` of 0 if any logical endpoint ID in the given range is not fully constructed, and a non-zero value otherwise.
